results.question: In what specific case is the network prohibited from using the NOTIFICATION message to re-establish user-plane resources for PDU sessions associated with non-3GPP access over 3GPP access?
results.reference: The network is prohibited if all the PDU sessions of the UE that are established over the 3GPP access are associated with control plane only indication.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.6.3.1, General
results.model_answer: The prohibition applies when the UE is in CM-IDLE state over non-3GPP access. In that case, the network shall not use a NOTIFICATION message sent over 3GPP access to re-establish user-plane resources for PDU sessions associated with non-3GPP access.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.4 (Notification procedure), normative restriction: the network shall not use the NOTIFICATION message to re-establish user-plane resources for PDU sessions associated with non-3GPP access over 3GPP access when the UE is in CM-IDLE state over non-3GPP access.

results.question: What three conditions must all be true for the network to be prohibited from using the NOTIFICATION message over non-3GPP access?
results.reference: The three conditions are: a) the MUSIM UE supports the paging indication for voice services, b) the network has indicated 'paging indication for voice services supported' to the UE, and c) the AMF detects that the downlink data is related to voice service.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.6.3.1, General
results.model_answer: The prohibition applies when all three are true: (1) the UE is in 5GMM-IDLE mode over non-3GPP access; (2) the UE is in MICO mode; and (3) the UE has not indicated support for N1-mode DRX. In that combination, the network must not send a NOTIFICATION message over non-3GPP access.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.3 (notification procedure / network-initiated notification over non-3GPP access). The normative text states that the network shall not send a NOTIFICATION message over non-3GPP access when the UE is in 5GMM-IDLE over non-3GPP access, is in MICO mode, and has not indicated support for N1-mode DRX.

results.question: Under what conditions must the SMF set the Authorized QoS rules IE in the PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND message when initiating a network-requested PDU session modification?
results.reference: The SMF must set the Authorized QoS rules IE when the authorized QoS rules of the PDU session are modified or are marked as to be synchronized with the UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.2.2, Network-requested PDU session modification procedure initiation
results.model_answer: The SMF shall include the Authorized QoS rules IE in a network-requested PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND when the modification changes the UE-authorized QoS-rule set for the PDU session—i.e., when one or more QoS rules are to be added, modified, or removed. The IE carries the affected rule operation(s). It is not required solely because other PDU-session parameters, such as Session-AMBR or QoS-flow descriptions, are changed, unless that change also requires a QoS-rule update.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.4.3.3 (network-requested PDU session modification), read with the PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND message specification in clause 8.3.3. The procedure specifies inclusion of Authorized QoS rules when the SMF modifies QoS rules for the PDU session; the IE encodes create/modify/delete operations for the applicable QoS rules.

results.question: How must the SMF handle service data flows for which the UE has requested traffic segregation if they have different QoS handling?
results.reference: The SMF must bind all these service data flows to a single QoS flow.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.2.2, Network-requested PDU session modification procedure initiation
results.model_answer: The SMF shall keep such service data flows segregated by providing separate QoS rules mapped to different QoS flows (i.e., different QFIs) for flows requiring different QoS handling. The applicable QoS rules shall carry the segregation indication as required for the UE-requested traffic segregation.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.7.1.1 (QoS rules), in the specification of the segregation and flow binding indication: QoS rules are used to associate service data flows with QoS flows, and traffic for which segregation is requested is indicated/handled separately where different QoS handling applies.

results.question: What must the SMF ensure regarding packet filters when setting the Authorized QoS rules IE for a PDU session?
results.reference: The SMF must ensure that the number of packet filters used in the authorized QoS rules does not exceed the maximum number of packet filters supported by the UE for that PDU session.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.2.2, Network-requested PDU session modification procedure initiation
results.model_answer: The SMF shall ensure that the same packet filter is not included in more than one QoS rule within the Authorized QoS rules IE for the PDU session.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.4.1.2 (UE-requested PDU session establishment procedure, construction of the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT ACCEPT). The normative requirement is that, when setting the Authorized QoS rules IE, the SMF ensures that a packet filter is not included in more than one QoS rule.

results.question: When the network-requested PDU session modification is triggered for P-CSCF restoration, and the UE had previously requested P-CSCF addresses which were provided, what must the SMF include in the Extended protocol configuration options IE?
results.reference: The SMF must include the P-CSCF IP address(es) in the Extended protocol configuration options IE of the PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.2.2, Network-requested PDU session modification procedure initiation
results.model_answer: The SMF shall include, in the Extended protocol configuration options (EPCO) IE, the P-CSCF IPv6 address and/or P-CSCF IPv4 address that the UE had previously requested and that the network had provided. The inclusion is conditional on the address family/families previously requested and supplied.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.4.3.3 (Network requested PDU session modification procedure; clause numbering may vary slightly by release/version): for P-CSCF restoration, when P-CSCF address(es) were previously requested by the UE and provided by the network, the SMF includes the relevant P-CSCF IPv6 address and/or P-CSCF IPv4 address in the EPCO IE.

results.question: What are the two distinct scenarios in which the AMF sets the PRTI IE in a RELAY KEY REJECT message, and what determines which value is used?
results.reference: The AMF sets the PRTI IE to either the PRTI value from the received RELAY KEY REQUEST message if the network decides to reject that request, or to the PRTI value from the received RELAY AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE message if the AMF receives an EAP-failure message from the AUSF.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.5.4.5, UE-initiated authentication and key agreement procedure not accepted by the network
results.model_answer: The two cases are rejection of a relay-key procedure for (1) 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay traffic and (2) 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay traffic. In each case, the AMF includes PRTI in RELAY KEY REJECT with the PRTI value corresponding to the relay traffic/procedure being rejected—i.e., the value associated with, and normally carried in, the triggering RELAY KEY REQUEST. The selection is therefore determined by the requested ProSe relay service type, not by the particular 5GMM reject cause.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.19.2 (ProSe relay key management / RELAY KEY REJECT handling), together with the PRTI IE definition in clause 9.11.3. The procedure text distinguishes UE-to-network-relay and UE-to-UE-relay key handling and requires the PRTI in the rejection to identify the applicable relay traffic type/transaction.

results.question: How does the content of the RELAY KEY REJECT message differ when the AMF receives an EAP-failure message from the AUSF compared to when the network decides to reject the RELAY KEY REQUEST?
results.reference: When the AMF receives an EAP-failure message from the AUSF, it includes the EAP message IE set with an EAP-failure message in the RELAY KEY REJECT message. When the network decides to reject the RELAY KEY REQUEST, there is no mention of including an EAP message IE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.5.4.5, UE-initiated authentication and key agreement procedure not accepted by the network
results.model_answer: If the AUSF returns EAP-Failure, the AMF sends RELAY KEY REJECT carrying the EAP message received from the AUSF, so that the UE can process the EAP failure. If the network locally decides to reject the RELAY KEY REQUEST, the AMF sends RELAY KEY REJECT with an appropriate 5GMM cause instead; it is not an AUSF EAP-failure payload.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4 (Relay key management procedure), in the AMF handling of the AUSF EAP result and of locally rejected RELAY KEY REQUESTs; corroborated by the RELAY KEY REJECT message-content specification in clause 8.2. The procedural distinction is: AUSF EAP-Failure -> include the received EAP message in RELAY KEY REJECT; network rejection -> include an appropriate 5GMM cause in RELAY KEY REJECT.

results.question: What are the sequential actions the AMF must take when the UE-initiated authentication and key agreement procedure is not accepted?
results.reference: The AMF must 1) create a RELAY KEY REJECT message, 2) set its PRTI IE based on the specific rejection scenario, and 3) send the RELAY KEY REJECT message to the UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.5.4.5, UE-initiated authentication and key agreement procedure not accepted by the network
results.model_answer: TS 24.501 treats AKA as network/AMF-initiated (not UE-initiated). Interpreting the question as the AMF not accepting the UE’s authentication result: the AMF shall (1) send an AUTHENTICATION REJECT message to the UE, (2) regard/abort the authentication procedure as failed, (3) release the NAS signalling connection, and (4) delete the UE’s 5G NAS security context, if one exists. The AUTHENTICATION REJECT causes the UE to invalidate its corresponding NAS security context and treat itself as deregistered.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.1.2.2 (Authentication procedure), together with clause 6.1.2.4 (Authentication reject procedure) (clause numbering/title can vary slightly by release). These specify the AMF behavior when authentication is not accepted and the AUTHENTICATION REJECT consequences.

results.question: What is the consequence for the UE upon receiving a RELAY KEY REJECT message, and what subsequent action must it take?
results.reference: The UE must consider the authentication has failed and must perform the PC5 signalling protocol procedure as specified in 3GPP 24.554 subclause 7.2.2.5.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.5.4.5, UE-initiated authentication and key agreement procedure not accepted by the network
results.model_answer: Upon receipt of a RELAY KEY REJECT message, the UE shall regard the UE-to-network relay key management procedure as failed. It shall then initiate UE-to-network relay reselection, i.e. seek/select another suitable relay rather than use the rejected relay for the requested relay connectivity.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, the "UE-to-network relay key management procedure" clause, UE handling of the RELAY KEY REJECT message. The normative outcome is that the procedure is considered failed and the UE initiates UE-to-network relay reselection.

results.question: How does the AMF determine the value of the non-3GPP implicit de-registration timer when T3346 is greater than the non-3GPP de-registration timer in specific NAS messages?
results.reference: The AMF sets the non-3GPP implicit de-registration timer value to be 8 minutes greater than the value of timer T3346 when T3346 is greater than the non-3GPP de-registration timer and the T3346 value IE is provided in DEREGISTRATION REQUEST (with 3GPP access type), REGISTRATION REJECT during mobility/periodic registration update, or SERVICE REJECT messages.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.3.7, Handling of the periodic registration update timer and mobile reachable timer
results.model_answer: For a network-initiated DEREGISTRATION REQUEST that carries both timers, the AMF uses T3346 as the lower bound. If the T3346 value is greater than the intended non-3GPP implicit de-registration timer value, the AMF shall set the non-3GPP de-registration timer to the T3346 value. Thus, the non-3GPP timer is not sent with a value shorter than T3346.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.5.2.3.3 (network-initiated deregistration procedure). The normative rule is that, when the DEREGISTRATION REQUEST includes the non-3GPP de-registration timer and T3346, if T3346 is greater than the non-3GPP de-registration timer value, the AMF shall set the non-3GPP de-registration timer value to the T3346 value.

results.question: Under what condition does the UE reset and start the non-3GPP de-registration timer, and when is this timer stopped?
results.reference: The UE registered over non-3GPP access resets and starts the non-3GPP de-registration timer when the N1 NAS signalling connection over non-3GPP access is released. The timer is stopped when certain NAS messages are received or when specific conditions are met, as indicated by the ellipsis in the clause.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.3.7, Handling of the periodic registration update timer and mobile reachable timer
results.model_answer: The UE resets and starts the non-3GPP de-registration timer when it is registered over both accesses and receives a REGISTRATION ACCEPT over 3GPP access that includes the Non-3GPP de-registration timer value IE. The timer is stopped when the UE receives a REGISTRATION ACCEPT over non-3GPP access. On expiry, the timer is used to trigger de-registration from non-3GPP access.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.5.1.2.4 (REGISTRATION ACCEPT message handling): the UE starts/resets the non-3GPP de-registration timer upon receipt, over 3GPP access, of a REGISTRATION ACCEPT containing the Non-3GPP de-registration timer value IE; it stops the timer upon receipt of a REGISTRATION ACCEPT over non-3GPP access.

results.question: How does the UE adjust the non-3GPP de-registration timer value when receiving T3346 in specific messages where T3346 exceeds the current timer value?
results.reference: The UE sets the non-3GPP de-registration timer value to be 4 minutes greater than the value of timer T3346 when it receives T3346 value IE in DEREGISTRATION REQUEST (with 3GPP access type), REGISTRATION REJECT during mobility/periodic registration update, or SERVICE REJECT messages and T3346 is greater than the current non-3GPP de-registration timer value.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.3.7, Handling of the periodic registration update timer and mobile reachable timer
results.model_answer: The UE shall restart T3346 with the received T3346 value when the received value is greater than the remaining value of the currently running T3346 for non-3GPP access. Thus, the back-off is extended to the new received duration; the UE does not merely add the new value to the remaining time. If the received value is not greater, the UE keeps the existing timer running unchanged.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.5.2.3.3 (UE behaviour on reception of a network-initiated DEREGISTRATION REQUEST), in the T3346 handling for non-3GPP access. The relevant normative rule is substantively: if T3346 is already running and the value in the received T3346 value IE is greater than the remaining value of T3346, the UE shall start/restart T3346 using the received value.

results.question: What triggers the AMF to start a non-3GPP implicit de-registration timer for a UE registered over non-3GPP access?
results.reference: The AMF starts a non-3GPP implicit de-registration timer for the UE registered over non-3GPP access when the N1 NAS signalling connection over non-3GPP access is released.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.3.7, Handling of the periodic registration update timer and mobile reachable timer
results.model_answer: The AMF starts the non-3GPP implicit de-registration timer when it receives the REGISTRATION COMPLETE message from a UE that is registered over non-3GPP access. In other words, the trigger is successful completion of the registration procedure, not merely receipt of the REGISTRATION REQUEST or transmission of REGISTRATION ACCEPT.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.3.2.4 (Registration complete procedure): for a UE registered over non-3GPP access, upon receipt of the REGISTRATION COMPLETE message, the AMF starts the non-3GPP implicit de-registration timer.

results.question: How does the network initiate the 5G AKA based primary authentication and key agreement procedure, and what are two mandatory information elements it must include in the initiating message?
results.reference: The network initiates the procedure by sending an AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message without the EAP message IE. It must include the ngKSI and the ABBA in that message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.3.1, General
results.model_answer: The network initiates 5G AKA primary authentication by sending an Authentication Request NAS message to the UE. For 5G AKA, the request mandatorily carries the Authentication parameter RAND and Authentication parameter AUTN (it also has mandatory ngKSI and ABBA fields in the Authentication Request format).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.1.2.2 (authentication and key agreement initiation): the network initiates the procedure by transmitting an Authentication Request message. The Authentication Request message format is specified in clause 8.2.1/Table 8.2.1; for 5G AKA it includes mandatory Authentication parameter RAND and Authentication parameter AUTN information elements.

results.question: What is the purpose of the 5G AKA based primary authentication and key agreement procedure, and what keys are agreed upon as a result?
results.reference: The purpose is to provide mutual authentication between the UE and the network and to agree on the keys KAUSF, KSEAF, and KAMF.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.3.1, General
results.model_answer: The 5G AKA-based primary authentication and key agreement procedure mutually authenticates the UE and the 5G network and establishes shared anchor keying material for subsequent access/NAS security. It results in agreement on K_AUSF (UE–AUSF anchor key) and K_SEAF (UE–SEAF/serving-network anchor key). K_AMF is subsequently derived from K_SEAF for the AMF/NAS security context; it is not the primary AKA anchor key itself.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.1.2 (5G AKA based primary authentication and key agreement procedure), read with clause 6.1.1 (general primary authentication): primary authentication provides mutual UE/network authentication and key agreement; the 5G AKA procedure establishes the K_AUSF and K_SEAF key hierarchy. The detailed 5G security-key derivations are specified in 3GPP TS 33.501 clause 6.1.

results.question: What condition must be met for the UE to proceed with a 5G authentication challenge, and what is established in both the UE and network upon successful authentication?
results.reference: The UE shall proceed only if a USIM is present. A partial native 5G NAS security context is established in both the UE and the network when authentication is successful.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.3.1, General
results.model_answer: The UE proceeds with the 5G authentication challenge only after successful verification of the authentication token AUTN (in particular, validation of its MAC, and freshness/SQN checks as applicable). If verification succeeds, the UE computes the authentication response (RES*) and key material. Following successful authentication, a common 5G security context—i.e., the mutually derived 5G security keys/context—is established in both the UE and the serving network.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.1.3.2 (Authentication request). It specifies that, on receiving AUTHENTICATION REQUEST, the UE verifies AUTN; if the MAC is valid, the UE calculates RES* and returns AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE. The authentication procedure in clause 6.1.3 establishes a 5G security context between the UE and network.

results.question: Following a successful 5G AKA primary authentication, what procedure must the AMF initiate and why is it initiated immediately?
results.reference: The AMF shall initiate a security mode control procedure to take the new partial native 5G NAS security context into use. It is initiated immediately to avoid KAUSF key mismatch between the UE and the network.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.3.1, General
results.model_answer: The AMF must initiate the NAS security mode control procedure by sending a SECURITY MODE COMMAND. It is initiated immediately after successful 5G AKA primary authentication so that the selected NAS integrity and ciphering algorithms are activated and the NAS security context is in use before any further NAS signalling/procedures are performed.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.7.2.1 (NAS security mode control procedure — General): the AMF initiates NAS security mode control after successful primary authentication/security-context establishment; it is done immediately to ensure NAS security is activated before subsequent NAS signalling.

results.question: How does the AMF initiate the network slice-specific EAP message reliable transport procedure?
results.reference: The AMF creates a NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION COMMAND message, sets the EAP message IE to the EAP-request message (generated by AMF or from AAA-S via NSSAAF), sets the S-NSSAI IE to the relevant HPLMN or SNPN S-NSSAI, sends the message, and starts timer T3575 per S-NSSAI.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.7.2.1, Network slice-specific EAP message reliable transport procedure initiation
results.model_answer: The AMF initiates the network slice-specific EAP message reliable transport procedure by sending a DL NAS TRANSPORT message to the UE. It sets the Payload container type to "EAP message", places the EAP-Request in the Payload container, includes the S-NSSAI identifying the slice concerned, and includes an EAP message identifier. The AMF starts T3580 after transmission; if the expected UL NAS TRANSPORT response carrying the corresponding identifier is not received before expiry, the AMF retransmits according to the procedure's retry rules.
results.evidence: Most likely clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.15.8.2.2, "Network slice-specific EAP message reliable transport procedure initiated by the AMF" (clause numbering can vary slightly by release). This clause specifies that the AMF sends DL NAS TRANSPORT with the EAP message, associated S-NSSAI and EAP message identifier, and starts timer T3580.

results.question: What two pieces of information does the UE pass to its upper layers upon receiving a NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION COMMAND message?
results.reference: The UE passes the EAP-request message from the EAP message IE and the HPLMN S-NSSAI or SNPN S-NSSAI from the S-NSSAI IE to the upper layers.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.7.2.1, Network slice-specific EAP message reliable transport procedure initiation
results.model_answer: The UE passes (1) the EAP message and (2) the S-NSSAI to its upper layers.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.15.8.2 (network slice-specific authentication and authorization procedure): “Upon receiving the NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION COMMAND message, the UE shall pass the EAP message and the S-NSSAI to the upper layers.”

results.question: What is the role of the S-NSSAI IE in the NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION COMMAND message during procedure initiation?
results.reference: The S-NSSAI IE is set by the AMF to the HPLMN S-NSSAI or the SNPN S-NSSAI to which the EAP-request message is related, identifying the specific network slice for the authentication.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.7.2.1, Network slice-specific EAP message reliable transport procedure initiation
results.model_answer: During initiation of network slice-specific authentication (NSSAA), the S-NSSAI IE identifies the specific network slice for which the NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION COMMAND requests authentication. It scopes/binds the command (including any EAP payload) to that S-NSSAI, enabling the UE to start or continue NSSAA for the correct slice rather than treating it as a general UE authentication request.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.15.9.2, "Network slice-specific authentication procedure initiation". The clause specifies that the network initiates NSSAA by sending a NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION COMMAND and includes the S-NSSAI IE to indicate the S-NSSAI for which the procedure is initiated. See also the NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION COMMAND message definition and the S-NSSAI IE definition in clause 9.11.2.

results.question: What immediate action does the UE take regarding timers when it receives a NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION COMMAND message?
results.reference: The UE stops timer T3346 if it is running, before passing the EAP-request and S-NSSAI to the upper layers.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.7.2.1, Network slice-specific EAP message reliable transport procedure initiation
results.model_answer: The UE shall stop timer T3580, if it is running.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.15.8.2 (network slice-specific authentication procedure, UE behaviour) states that, upon receipt of a NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION COMMAND message, the UE shall stop timer T3580 if running.

results.question: What is the purpose of the EAP message information element within the PDU SESSION AUTHENTICATION RESULT message in this procedure?
results.reference: To carry the final EAP packet (EAP Success or EAP Failure) that provides the result of the EAP authentication procedure, allowing the UE to report this result to the network.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.1.3, PDU EAP result message transport procedure
results.model_answer: The EAP message IE carries the network-side EAP packet to the UE’s EAP peer as part of PDU session authentication. In a PDU SESSION AUTHENTICATION RESULT, it is used to convey the terminating EAP outcome packet—normally EAP-Success or EAP-Failure—from the DN-AAA/EAP server (via the SMF) to the UE, so that the UE can complete the EAP exchange. It is NAS carriage for EAP and is distinct from the 5GSM cause, which conveys the 5GSM procedure outcome.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.3.2 (PDU session authentication procedure), read with the PDU SESSION AUTHENTICATION RESULT message definition in clause 8.3 and the EAP message IE definition in clause 9.11.4. The procedure specifies EAP packet exchange between UE and network/AAA using PDU SESSION AUTHENTICATION COMMAND, COMPLETE and RESULT messages; the RESULT message conveys the final EAP packet/result to the UE.

results.question: What specific action must the SMF take regarding timer T3592 upon receiving an indication that N1 SM delivery was skipped, and under what condition does this apply?
results.reference: The SMF shall stop timer T3592. This applies when the PDU SESSION RELEASE COMMAND message was sent along the N1 SM delivery skip allowed indication towards AMF and the SMF receives an indication that N1 SM delivery was skipped.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.3.4, N1 SM delivery skipped
results.model_answer: The SMF shall stop timer T3592 upon receiving an indication that N1 SM delivery was skipped. This applies when the skipped N1 SM message is a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND for which T3592 is running (i.e., the SMF is awaiting the UE's PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMPLETE).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.3.2.3 (network-requested PDU session modification): on receipt of an indication that N1 SM delivery was skipped, the SMF stops T3592, if it is running, for the applicable PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND procedure.

results.question: How should the SMF treat the state of the PDU session after receiving an indication of skipped N1 SM delivery following a specific message transmission?
results.reference: The SMF shall consider the PDU session as released. This occurs after the SMF sent the PDU SESSION RELEASE COMMAND message with the N1 SM delivery skip allowed indication and subsequently receives an indication that N1 SM delivery was skipped.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.3.4, N1 SM delivery skipped
results.model_answer: After the SMF has transmitted a PDU SESSION RELEASE COMMAND, an indication that N1 SM delivery was skipped is treated as completion of the release from the SMF perspective. The SMF shall consider the PDU session released and remove/release the corresponding PDU session context and associated resources; it does not wait for a PDU SESSION RELEASE COMPLETE from the UE.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.3.4.3 (Network-requested PDU Session Release): in the handling of the PDU SESSION RELEASE COMMAND, the specification states that, if the SMF receives an indication that N1 SM delivery was skipped, the SMF shall consider the PDU session released.

results.question: Describe the procedural consequence for the SMF when N1 SM delivery is skipped, given a prior transmission of the PDU SESSION RELEASE COMMAND message with a specific indication.
results.reference: The procedural consequence is twofold: the SMF shall stop timer T3592 and shall consider the PDU session as released. This is triggered by receiving an indication that N1 SM delivery was skipped, which follows the sending of the PDU SESSION RELEASE COMMAND message along the N1 SM delivery skip allowed indication towards the AMF.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.3.4, N1 SM delivery skipped
results.model_answer: If the SMF had sent the PDU SESSION RELEASE COMMAND with the PDU session release assistance indication and is informed that N1 SM delivery was skipped, it shall treat the PDU session release as completed. The SMF releases the PDU-session context/resources and does not wait for a PDU SESSION RELEASE COMPLETE from the UE.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.3.4.3 (network-initiated PDU session release): the rule associated with a PDU SESSION RELEASE COMMAND carrying the PDU session release assistance indication specifies that, when N1 SM delivery is skipped, the SMF considers the PDU session released.

results.question: What two definitive steps must the SMF perform upon being informed that N1 SM delivery was skipped, and what is the prerequisite message context for these steps?
results.reference: The SMF must stop timer T3592 and consider the PDU session as released. The prerequisite is that the SMF had previously sent the PDU SESSION RELEASE COMMAND message along the N1 SM delivery skip allowed indication towards the AMF.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.3.4, N1 SM delivery skipped
results.model_answer: Only when the skipped N1 SM message is a PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT ACCEPT, the SMF shall (1) release the PDU session and (2) inform the PCF that the PDU session has been released (where a PCF is associated/involved).
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.2.2.2 (UE-requested PDU session establishment). results.question: How does a UE in 5GMM-CONNECTED mode with RRC inactive indication process an access attempt upon detecting one of the events listed in subclause 4.5.1?
results.reference: The NAS categorizes the access attempt into access identities and an access category using either the standard tables and procedures (if not in SNPN mode) or the SNPN-specific tables and procedures (if in SNPN mode), and provides these to the lower layers for access control checking.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.5.4.2, Access control and checking in 5GMM-CONNECTED mode and in 5GMM-CONNECTED mode with RRC inactive indication
results.model_answer: The UE treats the trigger as an RRC-resume access attempt, not as a new 5GMM service-request transition. It determines the applicable access category and access identity for the detected event, provides them to the access-stratum procedures, and performs the applicable unified access-control/access-barring handling. If access is permitted, the UE initiates the RRC connection resume procedure; if barred, it does not resume until the barring conditions permit a later attempt.

The clause specifies the UE handling for events that trigger an access attempt, including determination/provision of access category and access identity. For a UE in 5GMM-CONNECTED mode with an RRC inactive indication, the corresponding access is made through RRC connection resume, with access control handled by the AS/RRC procedures.

results.question: What additional information can the NAS provide to the lower layers alongside the access identities and category when requesting access control checking for an event in connected mode?

results.question: How does the UE handle a request from upper layers to send a mobile originated location request when access control bars the associated access attempt in connected mode?
results.reference: The 5GMM shall not initiate the NAS transport procedure to send the LCS message. It may initiate the procedure later if the lower layers indicate the barring is alleviated for that access category and the message is still needed.

If the associated access attempt is barred, the UE shall not transmit the MO location request (i.e., no related UL NAS transport is sent) and shall indicate to upper layers that the request is barred/cannot be processed.

This clause specifies that, when upper layers request an MO location request, the UE performs the applicable access control; if the access attempt is barred, the UE informs upper layers accordingly rather than sending the request. Clause 5.6.1 provides the general access-control framework used for such access attempts.

results.question: How does the independence of 5GMM state machine instances between 3GPP and non-3GPP access impact UE registration status?
results.reference: The registration status and 5GMM parameters of the UE's 3GPP access and non-3GPP access 5GMM state machine instances are independent and can be different in each access.

results.model_answer: The UE maintains independent 5GMM state-machine instances for 3GPP and non-3GPP access. Therefore, registration is access-specific: the UE may be 5GMM-REGISTERED on 3GPP access while 5GMM-DEREGISTERED, registering, or deregistering on non-3GPP access, and vice versa. A registration, deregistration, mobility-management transition, or failure on one access does not by itself change the 5GMM registration state on the other access. Consequently, the UE can be simultaneously registered through both accesses, with separate registration contexts and procedure handling per access type.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.3.1.1 (5GMM states / general 5GMM state handling). It specifies that the UE maintains a separate 5GMM state machine for each access type and that the 5GMM state machines for 3GPP access and non-3GPP access are independent.

results.question: What actions must the AMF take regarding timer T3555 upon receiving a CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMPLETE message?

results.question: How does the AMF handle a new 5G-GUTI and TAI list received in a CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND message after the UE sends CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMPLETE?
results.reference: The AMF considers the new 5G-GUTI as valid and the old 5G-GUTI as invalid, and similarly considers the new TAI list as valid and the old TAI list as invalid.

Therefore, where the CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND contained a newly allocated 5G-GUTI and/or a TAI list, the AMF considers those delivered values valid for the UE; the new 5G-GUTI is the UE identity to be used subsequently, and the delivered TAI list is the UE's applicable registration-area information. CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMPLETE is only an acknowledgement—it does not carry the 5G-GUTI or TAI list back to the AMF.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.4.2 (network-initiated configuration update procedure): upon receipt of CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMPLETE, the AMF considers the configuration update procedure successfully completed and considers a new 5G-GUTI and/or TAI list sent in CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND to be valid.

results.question: What is the AMF's procedure when a new T3447 value is included in the CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND message and the UE completes the update?
results.reference: The AMF considers the T3447 value as valid. If the value is neither zero nor indicates deactivation, it uses this value the next time timer T3447 is started. If the value indicates deactivation or is zero, the AMF stops timer T3447 if it is running.

results.model_answer: On receipt of CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMPLETE, the AMF treats the configuration update as successfully completed, stops T3555 (if running), and commits/stores the new T3447 value that it sent in the CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND for that UE. The new T3447 value is therefore considered applicable only after successful completion of the update procedure.

results.question: Why is the 5GMM-NULL state considered the initial state for a UE's 5GMM mobility management?

In 5GMM-NULL the UE does not initiate 5GMM procedures; it subsequently moves to the appropriate operational state, typically 5GMM-DEREGISTERED, from which registration can be started. Thus, it represents initialization rather than an active registration or service state.

results.question: How does the network's knowledge of the UE differ when the UE is in the 5GMM-NULL state compared to other states?
results.reference: In the 5GMM-NULL state, the network has no knowledge of the UE's location or its 5GMM context, as the UE has not yet performed any registration.

In contrast, the non-NULL 5GMM states describe a UE that is at least identifiable in the 5GMM procedures/context model: 5GMM-REGISTERED means it is registered and network-reachable subject to CM state; 5GMM-DEREGISTERED means it is not registered, although it is a defined 5GMM state rather than the explicit “not known to the network” NULL condition.

results.question: Under what condition might the network include the local time zone information element during a procedure?

results.question: Why would a network send an AUTHENTICATION REJECT message to a UE that provided a 5G-GUTI mapped from an EPS GUTI?
results.reference: Because the network cannot retrieve the UE's subscription context using that identifier, which is a specified condition for sending the reject message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.5, Authentication reject
results.model_answer: A 5G-GUTI mapped from an EPS GUTI is not, by itself, a reason to reject authentication. It is a valid indication that the UE may be carrying an EPS-derived (mapped) 5GS security context and that the AMF may need to obtain the UE context from the EPS side (e.g. via interworking/context transfer). An AUTHENTICATION REJECT is appropriate if the network cannot successfully authenticate or authorize the UE—for example, the EPS-derived identity/context cannot be resolved and subsequent identity/authentication cannot be completed, the authentication response is invalid, or the home-network authentication result rejects the subscriber. The reject causes the UE to discard the relevant 5GMM/security context rather than continue using a potentially invalid mapped context. Thus, the operative reason is failed/unacceptable authentication, not merely the presence of a mapped 5G-GUTI.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.2 (Authentication procedure), including the network actions for AUTHENTICATION FAILURE/AUTHENTICATION REJECT. This procedure specifies that AUTHENTICATION REJECT is used when authentication is rejected/unsuccessful and that the UE clears its 5GMM security context on receipt. The registration and identity-handling rules in clause 5.5.1 further govern use of a 5G-GUTI, including one mapped from an EPS GUTI; they do not make such an identity alone an authentication-reject condition.

results.question: Under what condition does the network send the Emergency number list IE, and what geographical scope do the numbers in this list cover?

results.question: Under what conditions would a UE acting as a 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-network relay be prevented from initiating the remote UE report procedure?
results.reference: The UE is prevented from initiating the procedure if any of the timers T3396, T3584, or T3585 is running, as the clause explicitly states the UE shall not initiate the procedure while these timers are active.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.6.2.1, General
results.model_answer: A 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-network relay is prevented from initiating the remote UE report procedure when it is not authorized by the serving PLMN to provide the 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-network relay service. Practically, this includes receipt of a relay-service authorization indicating that the service is not allowed, or absence/withdrawal of the required authorization. The procedure also cannot be performed while the relay has no usable 5GS NAS service (for example, it is not normally registered/has only limited service), since the report must be sent to the network using NAS signalling.

The clause conditions initiation on the UE acting as a 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-network relay being authorized for the relay service; a UE not authorized for that service shall not initiate the procedure.

results.question: What is the functional purpose of the 5G ProSe remote UE report procedure as defined for a relay UE?
results.reference: The procedure's purpose is for a UE acting as a 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-network relay to notify the network about the connection status (connected or disconnected) of a 5G ProSe remote UE to that relay UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.6.2.1, General
results.model_answer: The ProSe remote UE report procedure enables a ProSe UE-to-network relay UE to inform the 5G network about remote UE(s) that are using, or have ceased using, the relay. Its functional purpose is to give the network visibility of the remote-UE-to-relay association and relevant remote-UE information, so that the network can maintain relay-service context and apply network functions such as authorization, policy, charging, and service continuity as applicable.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.27 (ProSe), most likely the subclause titled "ProSe remote UE report procedure" under the ProSe UE-to-network relay procedures (commonly numbered around clause 5.27.5.x, depending on release). The procedure specifies reporting by the relay UE to the network of remote UE information/association for remote UEs served through that relay.

results.question: How does the specification restrict the initiation of the remote UE report procedure in relation to specific timers?
results.reference: The specification imposes a restriction by prohibiting the UE from initiating the procedure if timer T3396 is running, if timer T3584 is running, or if timer T3585 is running.

results.question: For what specific events related to a remote UE must a 5G ProSe layer-3 relay UE notify the network?
results.reference: The relay UE must notify the network when a 5G ProSe remote UE becomes connected to it or becomes disconnected from it, as this is the defined purpose of the report procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.6.2.1, General
results.model_answer: A 5G ProSe layer-3 relay UE must notify the network when a remote UE's connectivity via that relay changes: (1) the remote UE becomes reachable via the relay, i.e. it establishes the PC5 unicast connection/relay association; and (2) the remote UE becomes unreachable via the relay, i.e. that PC5 connection/association is released or lost. A change of relay is represented by the old relay reporting the remote UE unreachable and the new relay reporting it reachable.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, the clause titled "5G ProSe layer 3 UE-to-network relay" (Remote UE reporting / relay-specific NAS handling; subclause numbering is release-dependent). Its normative requirement is that the relay reports to the network when a remote UE becomes reachable or unreachable through that 5G ProSe L3 relay UE.

results.question: What specific actions must the UE take if it detects that the ngKSI received in the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message is already in use?
results.reference: The UE shall send an AUTHENTICATION FAILURE message to the network with the 5GMM cause #71 'ngKSI already in use' and then follow the procedure described in subclause 5.4.1.3.7, item e.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.3.6, Authentication not accepted by the UE
results.model_answer: The UE shall reject the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST and send an AUTHENTICATION FAILURE message with 5GMM cause #71, "ngKSI already in use." It must not accept the received ngKSI for a new authentication/security context.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.2.2 (authentication procedure, UE handling of AUTHENTICATION REQUEST): if the ngKSI received in an AUTHENTICATION REQUEST is already in use, the UE shall send an AUTHENTICATION FAILURE message with 5GMM cause #71 "ngKSI already in use."

results.question: How does the UE handle a scenario where it finds the MAC code supplied by the core network in the AUTN parameter to be invalid?
results.reference: The UE shall send an AUTHENTICATION FAILURE message to the network with the 5GMM cause #20 'MAC failure' and then follow the procedure described in subclause 5.4.1.3.7, item c.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.3.6, Authentication not accepted by the UE
results.model_answer: The UE rejects the authentication challenge and sends an AUTHENTICATION FAILURE message to the AMF with 5GMM cause #20, "MAC failure." It does not perform SQN resynchronization or include an AUTS/Authentication Failure Parameter, since AUTS is used only when the MAC is valid but synchronization fails.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.1.3.2 (authentication procedure): if the UE finds that the MAC code in the AUTN parameter is not valid, it shall send an AUTHENTICATION FAILURE message with 5GMM cause #20 "MAC failure" to the AMF.

results.question: What are the UE's required actions upon returning an AUTHENTICATION FAILURE message to the network for any reason?
results.reference: The UE shall delete any previously stored RAND and RES* and shall stop timer T3516, if running.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.3.6, Authentication not accepted by the UE
results.model_answer: After sending AUTHENTICATION FAILURE for any cause, the UE shall delete any existing 5G NAS security context and set the ngKSI to "no key is available".
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.2.3 (UE behaviour): "Upon returning an AUTHENTICATION FAILURE message to the network for any reason, the UE shall delete the 5G NAS security context, if any, and shall set the ngKSI to 'no key is available'."

results.question: What procedure does the UE follow when it finds the sequence number SQN supplied by the core network in the AUTN parameter to be out of range?
results.reference: The UE shall send an AUTHENTICATION FAILURE message to the network with the 5GMM cause #21 'synch failure' and include a re-synchronization token AUTS provided by the USIM, then follow the procedure described in subclause 5.4.1.3.7, item f.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.3.6, Authentication not accepted by the UE
results.model_answer: The UE treats this as an AKA synchronization failure. It sends an AUTHENTICATION FAILURE NAS message with 5GMM cause #21 "synch failure" and includes the Authentication failure parameter IE containing AUTS, generated by the USIM. AUTS enables the network to resynchronize its SQN with the UE; the UE does not return RES* for that AUTN.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.1.3.2 (Authentication procedure): when the UE detects that the SQN in AUTN is out of range, it shall send an AUTHENTICATION FAILURE message with 5GMM cause #21 "synch failure" and include the AUTS parameter in the Authentication failure parameter IE.

results.question: Under what condition is the Extended protocol configuration options IE included in a message according to clause 8.3.7.9?
results.reference: It is included when the UE needs to transmit protocol data to the network.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.7.9, Extended protocol configuration options
results.model_answer: The Extended protocol configuration options IE may be included only when the Protocol configuration options IE is also included in the same message. This is a necessary co-presence condition; inclusion of the Protocol configuration options IE does not by itself require inclusion of the Extended IE.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 8.3.7.9 (Extended protocol configuration options): "The Extended protocol configuration options IE shall be included in a message only if the Protocol configuration options IE is included in the same message."

results.question: What is the purpose of the Extended protocol configuration options IE as defined in clause 8.3.7.9?
results.reference: Its purpose is to allow the UE to send protocol data, such as configuration parameters, error codes, or messages/events, to the network.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.7.9, Extended protocol configuration options
results.model_answer: The Extended protocol configuration options (EPCO) IE carries protocol-configuration options between the UE and the network when the normal Protocol configuration options (PCO) IE is not large enough to carry all required options. It therefore provides an extended-length transport for the same type of protocol/application/IP configuration information.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 8.3.7.9, defines the Extended protocol configuration options IE for transferring protocol configuration options between UE and network when those options cannot be transferred using the Protocol configuration options IE because of the latter's length limitation.

results.question: What types of protocol data can the UE transmit to the network using the Extended protocol configuration options IE?
results.reference: The UE can transmit configuration parameters, error codes, or messages/events.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.7.9, Extended protocol configuration options
results.model_answer: The UE can use the Extended protocol configuration options (EPCO) IE to transfer protocol-configuration data for PPP, IP, DHCPv4, and DHCPv6. The IE carries protocol/container options for the selected configuration protocol; it is not a general-purpose NAS data container.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 10.5.6.3, "Extended protocol configuration options IE": the Configuration protocol field identifies the protocol configuration data as PPP, IP, DHCPv4, or DHCPv6.

results.question: What specific action should a UE take if it receives a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND message for a PDU session that is currently in the PDU SESSION INACTIVE state?
results.reference: The UE shall set the 5GSM cause IE to #43 'Invalid PDU session identity' in a 5GSM STATUS message, include the received PDU session ID in the UL NAS TRANSPORT message, and send it as specified in subclause 5.4.5.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.2.6, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: The UE shall send a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION REJECT message, with 5GSM cause #43, "invalid PDU session identity." It shall not apply the requested modification or transition the PDU session to active.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.4.3.3 (network-requested PDU session modification). The UE handling for a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND associated with a PDU session in the PDU SESSION INACTIVE state requires a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION REJECT with 5GSM cause #43 (invalid PDU session identity).

results.question: How does the UE resolve a collision when it receives a network-initiated PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND for the same PDU session during its own UE-requested modification procedure?
results.reference: The UE shall abort its internal UE-requested procedure, transition the PDU session to the ACTIVE state, and proceed with executing the network-requested PDU session modification procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.2.6, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: The UE gives precedence to the network-initiated procedure. It aborts the ongoing UE-requested PDU session modification for that PDU session (including stopping its associated retransmission handling), processes the received PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND, and sends PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMPLETE as applicable. The UE must not re-initiate its UE-requested modification until the network-requested modification procedure has completed; it may initiate a new request afterward if the requested change is still needed.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.4.3.3 (UE-requested PDU session modification procedure), collision handling. The normative collision rule is that, upon receipt of a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND for a PDU session for which a UE-requested modification is ongoing, the UE aborts the UE-requested procedure and proceeds with the network-requested modification procedure; it does not re-initiate the UE-requested procedure before completion of the network-requested procedure.

results.question: Under what condition regarding the PTI IE in a received PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND message triggers the UE to handle a collision with its own ongoing procedure?
results.reference: The condition is when the PTI IE in the received message is set to 'No procedure transaction identity assigned' and the message is for the same PDU session the UE is currently trying to modify.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.2.6, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: The UE treats the received PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND as colliding with its own ongoing UE-initiated procedure when the command contains a PTI IE whose value is a UE-assigned PTI and that PTI matches the PTI of an ongoing UE-initiated PDU session modification procedure for the same PDU session.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.4.3.4 (PDU session modification procedure initiated by the network), UE handling of PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND: the collision case is identified from a PTI IE carrying a PTI value assigned by the UE that corresponds to the UE's ongoing PDU session modification procedure.

results.question: What is the complete UE behavior, including message construction and cause code, when identifying a PDU session ID in a modification command that corresponds to an inactive session?
results.reference: The UE constructs a 5GSM STATUS message with the 5GSM cause IE set to #43, uses the received PDU session ID, and sends it via an UL NAS TRANSPORT message as defined in the referenced subclause.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.2.6, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: On receiving a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND whose PDU session ID is mapped by the UE to a PDU session in the PDU SESSION INACTIVE state, the UE shall not apply the requested modification. It shall return a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND REJECT, using the PDU session ID (and the procedure transaction identity) from the received command, and include the mandatory 5GSM cause IE set to cause #54, "PDU session does not exist." The session remains inactive.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.4.2.3 (network-requested PDU session modification): the UE behavior for a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND identifying a PDU session in the PDU SESSION INACTIVE state is to send PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND REJECT with 5GSM cause #54 "PDU session does not exist."

results.question: What action should the AMF take when a UE initiates a de-registration procedure in a cell belonging to an SNPN with a non-globally-unique SNPN identity for which the UE has no valid subscription, and the procedure is not due to 'switch off'?
results.reference: The network shall initiate the de-registration procedure, and the AMF shall send a DEREGISTRATION REQUEST message including the 5GMM cause #74 'Temporarily not authorized for this SNPN'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.5.2.2.7, Abnormal cases in the network side
results.model_answer: The AMF shall accept and complete the UE-initiated deregistration: it deregisters the UE and, because the deregistration is not for "switch off", sends a DEREGISTRATION ACCEPT to the UE. The lack of a valid subscription for the non-globally-unique SNPN does not result in a DEREGISTRATION REJECT (no such 5GMM message exists for this procedure).
results.evidence: Most likely TS 24.501 clause: 5.5.2.2.2, "Deregistration procedure initiated by the UE" (AMF behaviour). This clause specifies that, after processing a UE-originated DEREGISTRATION REQUEST, the AMF deregisters the UE and sends DEREGISTRATION ACCEPT when the UE did not indicate deregistration due to switch-off. The SNPN/non-globally-unique-SNPN subscription condition is handled within this UE-originated deregistration handling rather than by rejecting the request.

results.question: How does the network respond when a UE initiates a de-registration procedure in a cell belonging to an SNPN with a globally-unique SNPN identity for which the UE has no valid subscription, and the de-registration is not due to 'switch off'?
results.reference: The network shall initiate the de-registration procedure, and the AMF shall send a DEREGISTRATION REQUEST message including the 5GMM cause #75 'Permanently not authorized for this SNPN'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.5.2.2.7, Abnormal cases in the network side
results.model_answer: The network acknowledges the UE-originated de-registration by sending a DEREGISTRATION ACCEPT message. The lack of a valid subscription for the globally-unique SNPN does not, by itself, change the de-registration acknowledgement into a rejection. The exception is a DEREGISTRATION REQUEST indicating "switch off"; in that case no DEREGISTRATION ACCEPT is returned.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.5.2.2.2 (UE-initiated deregistration procedure accepted by the network / network behaviour). It specifies that the network sends a DEREGISTRATION ACCEPT to acknowledge UE-originated deregistration; the explicit no-response exception is when the deregistration type indicates "switch off". The SNPN/no-valid-subscription condition does not override that acknowledgement for a non-switch-off deregistration.

results.question: How should the network handle a scenario where it receives a REGISTRATION REQUEST message for initial or emergency registration from a UE before a UE-initiated de-registration procedure (not due to switch off) has been completed?
results.reference: The network shall abort the de-registration procedure and progress the registration procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.5.2.2.7, Abnormal cases in the network side
results.model_answer: The network shall abort the ongoing UE-initiated de-registration procedure (when it is not due to switch-off) and handle the received REGISTRATION REQUEST for initial registration or emergency registration.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.5.2.2 (UE-initiated de-registration procedure): "If the network receives a REGISTRATION REQUEST message for initial registration or emergency registration from a UE before the UE-initiated de-registration procedure (not due to switch off) has been completed, the network shall abort the UE-initiated de-registration procedure and handle the REGISTRATION REQUEST message."

results.question: What specific actions must a UE perform upon receiving a ProSe direct link establishment request from a 5G ProSe remote UE that includes the SUCI, when establishing a secure PC5 unicast link with security performed over control plane?
results.reference: The UE must allocate a PRTI value, create a RELAY KEY REQUEST message, set the PRTI IE to the allocated value, set the relay key request parameters IE with the received SUCI, relay service code, and nonce_1, send the message, and start timer T35xx upon sending.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.5.4.3, UE-initiated authentication and key agreement procedure initiation
results.model_answer: The receiving 5G ProSe UE shall not treat the received SUCI as a PC5 key or attempt to de-conceal it. For the control-plane-security variant, it shall forward the received SUCI to its serving AMF in a NAS PROSE DIRECT LINK ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST, so that the 5GS can identify/authorize the requesting remote UE and provide the required PC5-unicast security information. The UE shall wait for the corresponding 5GS result/security context, establish the PC5 unicast security context using the received 5GS-provided parameters, and then send the PC5 ProSe Direct Link Establishment Accept to the remote UE. If the 5GS rejects the request or security establishment fails, it shall reject/fail the PC5 direct-link establishment rather than establish a secure link.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.20.2.2 (PC5 unicast/direct link establishment), in the procedure case where PC5 unicast security is performed over the control plane. The normative behavior is the forwarding of the SUCI received in the PC5 ProSe Direct Link Establishment Request in a NAS PROSE DIRECT LINK ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST to the AMF, followed by use of the 5GS result/security information before accepting the PC5 link.

results.question: How does the UE populate the RELAY KEY REQUEST message after allocating a PRTI value during the UE-initiated authentication and key agreement procedure?
results.reference: The UE sets the PRTI IE of the message to the allocated PRTI value and sets the relay key request parameters IE with the SUCI, relay service code, and nonce_1 received from the 5G ProSe remote UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.5.4.3, UE-initiated authentication and key agreement procedure initiation
results.model_answer: The UE creates a RELAY KEY REQUEST with the normal 5GMM NAS header and sets the PRTI IE to the newly allocated ProSe Relay Transaction Identifier value. It includes the other request/relay-identification information required by the RELAY KEY REQUEST message definition and applies NAS security protection when a usable NAS security context exists. The PRTI is retained by the UE to correlate the subsequent UE-initiated AKA signalling and the resulting relay-key response; the UE does not place a derived relay key in the request.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.3 subclause titled "UE-initiated authentication and key agreement procedure", together with the RELAY KEY REQUEST message-content specification in clause 8. The procedure text requires allocation of a PRTI and inclusion of that allocated value in the RELAY KEY REQUEST.

results.question: Following the creation and configuration of the RELAY KEY REQUEST message, what are the final two procedural steps the UE must execute?
results.reference: The UE must send the RELAY KEY REQUEST message and then start the timer T35xx upon sending that message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.5.4.3, UE-initiated authentication and key agreement procedure initiation
results.model_answer: The UE shall (1) send the configured RELAY KEY REQUEST message to the AMF, and (2) start timer T3586 to supervise receipt of the corresponding relay-key response.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.17 (5G ProSe/UE-to-network relay procedures), in the Relay key request procedure. The UE-side procedure concludes by transmitting the RELAY KEY REQUEST to the AMF and starting T3586.

results.question: What information from the 5G ProSe remote UE must be included in the relay key request parameters IE of the RELAY KEY REQUEST message?
results.reference: The relay key request parameters IE must be set with the SUCI, relay service code, and nonce_1 received from the 5G ProSe remote UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.5.4.3, UE-initiated authentication and key agreement procedure initiation
results.model_answer: The RELAY KEY REQUEST shall include the 5G ProSe remote UE ID in the Relay key request parameters IE. This identifies the remote UE for which relay key material is requested.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.19 (5G ProSe UE-to-network relay key-management procedure), in the RELAY KEY REQUEST transmission step: the relay UE includes the 5G ProSe remote UE ID in the Relay key request parameters IE.

results.question: Under what condition is the Remote UE handling information list IE included in a message?
results.reference: When the UE needs to transmit an EAP message to a 5G ProSe layer-3 remote UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.5.3, Remote UE handling information list
results.model_answer: The Remote UE handling information list IE is included only when the receiving UE is acting as a 5G ProSe UE-to-Network Relay and the AMF has Remote-UE-specific handling information to provide for one or more Remote UEs served by that relay. It is therefore conditional/optional and is not included for an ordinary UE or merely because the recipient is a Remote UE.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.4 (configuration update procedure), together with the applicable NAS message-content table for CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND. The inclusion condition is expressed in terms of the UE being a UE-to-Network Relay and the network/AMF having Remote UE handling information to deliver.

results.question: What is the purpose of including the Remote UE handling information list IE in a message?
results.reference: To facilitate the transmission of an EAP message from the UE to a 5G ProSe layer-3 remote UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.5.3, Remote UE handling information list
results.model_answer: The Remote UE handling information list IE is used to convey, for each Remote UE associated with a UE-to-network relay, the handling information/action that the 5GS shall apply to that Remote UE. It enables the network (notably the AMF) to maintain and manage the Remote UE's 5GS context, reachability and association through the relay, including corresponding update or release handling where applicable.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 9.11.3, IE definition "Remote UE handling information list": the IE carries a list of Remote UE handling information entries and is intended to indicate to the network the handling to be performed for Remote UE(s). The applicable 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay procedures in TS 24.501 clause 5.17 provide the procedural context for using this information.

results.question: What specific type of remote UE is targeted when the Remote UE handling information list IE is used?
results.reference: A 5G ProSe layer-3 remote UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.5.3, Remote UE handling information list
results.model_answer: It targets Remote UEs in 5GMM-CM-IDLE that are connected to the 5G system through a UE-to-Network Relay UE. It is not a general list for arbitrary ProSe Remote UEs or for the relay UE itself.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 9.11.3, the IE definition entitled "Remote UE handling information list". The IE is specified for conveying handling information associated with Remote UE(s) in CM-IDLE served via a UE-to-Network Relay UE.

results.question: Under what conditions does the AMF include the Configured NSSAI IE when providing a new configured NSSAI for the current PLMN?
results.reference: The AMF includes the Configured NSSAI IE when it needs to provide a new configured NSSAI for the current PLMN and the UE is neither registering nor registered for onboarding services in an SNPN.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.19.15, Configured NSSAI
results.model_answer: The AMF includes the Configured NSSAI IE when it has determined that the UE is to receive a new (i.e. updated or replacement) Configured NSSAI for the current PLMN. During a registration procedure, it carries that new list in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message. If the UE is already registered and the AMF subsequently needs to change the Configured NSSAI, it provides it using the CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND procedure. The condition is a change/determination of the UE’s PLMN-specific Configured NSSAI, not merely a change in the Allowed NSSAI for one registration.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.15.4.1 (Configured NSSAI / general NSSAI handling), read with clause 5.5.1.2.4 (REGISTRATION ACCEPT handling) and clause 5.5.1.3 (Configuration update procedure). These specify that the AMF provides a Configured NSSAI for the current PLMN when it determines a new Configured NSSAI, using REGISTRATION ACCEPT during registration or CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND otherwise.

results.question: Why would the AMF send the Configured NSSAI IE to the UE for the current SNPN?
results.reference: The AMF sends the Configured NSSAI IE to provide the UE with a new configured NSSAI for the current SNPN, but this action is conditional on the UE not being involved in SNPN onboarding services.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.19.15, Configured NSSAI
results.model_answer: The AMF sends Configured NSSAI to provision or refresh the UE's NSSAI configuration specifically associated with the currently selected SNPN (i.e., the PLMN identity together with its NID). This tells the UE which S-NSSAIs it should retain and use as its configured slice set when operating in that SNPN, including for later Requested NSSAI construction. It is SNPN-specific because a Configured NSSAI for another PLMN or another SNPN must not be assumed applicable. This is distinct from Allowed NSSAI: Allowed NSSAI is the slice set authorized for the current registration, whereas Configured NSSAI is UE configuration for the current SNPN. The AMF would include it when it needs to install, replace, or synchronize the UE's stored configuration with the network's configuration for that SNPN.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.15.4.1 (NSSAI handling, general), read with the REGISTRATION ACCEPT procedure in clause 4.2.2.2. The clause specifies UE handling/storage of Configured NSSAI in association with the current PLMN; for SNPN operation this association is with the current SNPN. Therefore, a Configured NSSAI received from the AMF is used to update the UE's configuration for that specific serving SNPN, rather than as a generic or roaming-wide NSSAI configuration.

results.question: Under what conditions is the use of the 'null integrity protection algorithm' 5G-IA0 allowed in the current 5G NAS security context?
results.reference: It is only allowed for three specific cases: a) for an unauthenticated UE for which establishment of emergency services is allowed, b) for a W-AGF acting on behalf of an FN-RG, and c) for a W-AGF acting on behalf of an N5GC device.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.4.4.1, General
results.model_answer: 5G-IA0 is not a normal selectable NAS integrity algorithm. In a current 5G NAS security context, it is allowed only when the UE security capability associated with that context indicates no supported non-null 5G NAS integrity algorithm (i.e. no 5G-IA1, 5G-IA2 or 5G-IA3). The exceptional case is limited-service emergency operation: the UE may accept/use 5G-IA0 for an emergency registration while in limited service, even where stronger integrity algorithms are supported. Thus, an AMF must not downgrade an ordinary registered UE with available non-null integrity capability to 5G-IA0.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.2 (NAS security mode control), in particular the SECURITY MODE COMMAND processing requirements: the UE is required to reject selection of 5G-IA0 when it has indicated support for a non-null 5G NAS integrity algorithm, except for the limited-service/emergency-registration case. The relevant comparison is against the UE security capability retained/used in the current 5G NAS security context.

results.question: How should the UE and AMF set the security header type in outbound NAS messages when the 'null integrity protection algorithm' is indicated in the security context?
results.reference: They shall apply the same rules irrespective of whether the 'null integrity protection algorithm' or any other integrity protection algorithm is indicated in the 5G NAS security context.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.4.4.1, General
results.model_answer: The UE and AMF shall set the Security Header Type (SHT) to "integrity protected" (value 1) in outbound NAS messages when the security context indicates the null integrity protection algorithm (NIA0). They shall not send such messages as plain NAS messages merely because NIA0 provides no cryptographic integrity protection.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 4.4.3.1 (NAS security header / Security header type). It specifies that, if the null integrity protection algorithm is indicated in the security context, the UE and AMF shall set the security header type in the NAS message to "integrity protected".

results.question: What is the processing order when a NAS message needs to be sent both ciphered and integrity protected?
results.reference: The NAS message is first ciphered, and then the ciphered NAS message and the NAS sequence number are integrity protected by calculating the MAC.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.4.4.1, General
results.model_answer: Cipher first, then integrity-protect. The sender encrypts the NAS message payload using the selected NAS ciphering algorithm and then computes/appends the NAS MAC using the selected integrity algorithm over the security-protected message inputs, including the sequence number and ciphered payload. The receiver verifies integrity before accepting/deciphering the payload.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 4.4 (NAS security), in the security-protected NAS message processing requirements: where both ciphering and integrity protection apply, ciphering is performed before integrity protection (i.e., integrity protection covers the ciphered NAS message).

results.question: How is integrity protection handled when a 5GSM message is piggybacked in a 5GMM message?
results.reference: There is only one Sequence number IE and one Message authentication code IE for the 5GMM message that is piggybacking the 5GSM message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.4.4.1, General
results.model_answer: A piggybacked 5GSM message is not integrity-protected independently. It is carried as part of the 5GMM message (typically in a NAS message container/payload container), and the NAS integrity protection of the enclosing 5GMM message covers the embedded 5GSM bytes. Thus, if the outer 5GMM message is integrity protected, the piggybacked 5GSM message is protected by the same NAS MAC and UE-AMF NAS security context; if the outer message is sent unprotected under an allowed exception, piggybacking does not add separate 5GSM integrity protection.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 4.4.1 (General, NAS security), which specifies that a 5GSM message piggybacked in a 5GMM message is integrity protected together with the 5GMM message. Related mechanics are specified in the NAS security-header/security-protected NAS-message clauses of 4.4.

results.question: Under what condition would a network include the Extended CAG information list IE towards a UE?
results.reference: The network may include this IE when the UE supports Extended CAG information list, for the purpose of either assigning a new CAG information list to the UE or deleting the existing CAG information list at the UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.19.32, Extended CAG information list
results.model_answer: A network includes the Extended CAG information list IE only for a UE that has requested CAG-information-list delivery and has indicated support for the extended CAG-information-list format, when the network has applicable CAG information to provide (in particular, where the extended representation is needed/selected instead of the legacy CAG information list). UE support is the essential interoperability gate; the IE is not sent merely because the UE is camped on, or registered through, a CAG cell.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.5.1.2.4 (REGISTRATION ACCEPT message content / CAG information handling). The AMF's inclusion of CAG-information-list information is conditional on the UE's CAG information list request and UE support for the relevant (extended) CAG information list capability/format. Related Configuration Update procedures apply the same UE-capability constraint when updating CAG information.

results.question: How is the 5GMM-REGISTERED state structured according to the 5GMM sublayer state machine?
results.reference: The 5GMM-REGISTERED state is subdivided into a number of substates as described in the referenced subclause.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.1.3.2.1.4.1, General
results.model_answer: The 5GMM-REGISTERED state is a parent 5GMM state divided into six substates: 5GMM-REGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE, 5GMM-REGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-REGISTRATION-UPDATE, 5GMM-REGISTERED.LIMITED-SERVICE, 5GMM-REGISTERED.NO-CELL-AVAILABLE, 5GMM-REGISTERED.PLMN-SEARCH, and 5GMM-REGISTERED.SUSPENDED. These substates distinguish whether normal or limited service is available, a registration update is being attempted, no cell is available, PLMN selection/search is in progress, or 5GMM operation is suspended.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.3.1.3, "5GMM-REGISTERED state". This clause defines 5GMM-REGISTERED as comprising the listed substates in the 5GMM sublayer state machine.

results.question: Why are certain 5GMM-REGISTERED substates not relevant for a UE accessing the network via a non-3GPP access type?
results.reference: The substates described in the subclause are not applicable to non-3GPP access, meaning they are defined only for 3GPP access procedures.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.1.3.2.1.4.1, General
results.model_answer: These substates model 3GPP radio-access conditions: camping on a cell, PLMN/cell search, absence of a suitable cell, limited service on a cell, and attempts to update registration while such 3GPP conditions apply.
