The NAS COMPLETE message itself does not constitute NSSAA success; the NSSAAF result determines the authorization outcome.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.15.9.2 (Network slice-specific authentication procedure): AMF handling of NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION COMPLETE includes handling an HPLMN S-NSSAI by mapping it to the corresponding VPLMN S-NSSAI and relaying the EAP message to the NSSAAF associated with the slice-specific authentication procedure.

results.question: Why is the network slice-specific authentication and authorization procedure considered transparent to the UE's 5GMM layer after sending the NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION COMPLETE message?
results.reference: Apart from sending the message, the procedure does not involve further actions at the 5GMM layer, meaning it operates without additional 5GMM layer processing.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.7.2.2, Network slice-specific EAP message reliable transport procedure accepted by the UE
results.model_answer: Because NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION COMPLETE is the UE's last 5GMM-visible contribution to NSSAA. After transmitting it, the UE has delivered the slice-specific authentication payload/result toward the network; any remaining EAP/AAA processing and the authorization decision are handled outside the UE 5GMM state machine. The UE 5GMM layer neither waits for nor interprets a separate NSSAA success/failure outcome. Any later effect on usable S-NSSAIs is conveyed through normal NAS mechanisms, e.g. Registration Accept or Configuration Update, rather than as further UE-5GMM NSSAA processing.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.15.2 (Network slice-specific authentication and authorization procedure), UE behaviour: "After the UE has sent the NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION COMPLETE message, the network slice-specific authentication and authorization procedure is transparent to the UE's 5GMM layer." This establishes that subsequent slice-authentication processing is not a UE 5GMM procedure/state-machine concern.

results.question: How does the UE determine the content of the S-NSSAI IE in the NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION COMPLETE message?
results.reference: The UE sets the S-NSSAI IE to the specific HPLMN S-NSSAI or SNPN S-NSSAI that is associated with the EAP-response message provided by upper layers.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.7.2.2, Network slice-specific EAP message reliable transport procedure accepted by the UE
results.model_answer: The UE copies the S-NSSAI value from the NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION COMMAND associated with the completed network slice-specific authentication procedure. Thus, the S-NSSAI IE in NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION COMPLETE identifies the same S-NSSAI for which the UE has just completed NSSAA; it is not independently selected from the UE's Allowed/Configured NSSAI.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.15.7.2 (network slice-specific authentication procedure at the UE). The UE sends NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION COMPLETE after successful completion of the authentication exchange and includes the S-NSSAI identifying the slice for which the NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION COMMAND was received. The message-format clause for NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION COMPLETE provides the corresponding S-NSSAI IE requirement.

results.question: Under what specific conditions is the AMF prohibited from rejecting 5GMM signalling requests when general NAS level congestion control is active?
results.reference: The AMF must not reject requests for emergency services, emergency services fallback, requests from UEs configured for high priority access in the selected PLMN, DEREGISTRATION REQUEST messages, requests for mobile terminated services triggered by paging or notification, and requests for initial registration or mobility/periodic registration updates when emergency is indicated by lower layers.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.3.9, Handling of NAS level mobility management congestion control
results.model_answer: With general NAS-level congestion control active, the AMF must not reject a 5GMM request on congestion grounds when it is an emergency or priority-protected request: (1) a REGISTRATION REQUEST for emergency registration; (2) a SERVICE REQUEST whose service type is "emergency services" or "emergency fallback"; (3) a SERVICE REQUEST for "high priority access" (e.g., MPS/MCS priority use); and (4) a UE-initiated DEREGISTRATION REQUEST. These requests are exempt from congestion rejection; ordinary registration/service requests may otherwise be congestion-controlled.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.3.7.2 (general NAS level congestion control). The clause specifies the 5GMM signalling requests that the AMF shall not reject during general NAS-level congestion control, including emergency registration, emergency/emergency-fallback service, high-priority-access service, and UE-initiated deregistration.

results.question: How should the AMF select the value for timer T3346 when rejecting UEs during congestion control, and what is the purpose of this selection method?
results.reference: The AMF should select the T3346 value for rejected UEs so that timeouts are not synchronized. This is done to prevent large numbers of UEs from simultaneously initiating deferred requests after the timer expires.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.3.9, Handling of NAS level mobility management congestion control
results.model_answer: For each congestion-related rejection, the AMF should independently/randomly select the T3346 back-off value from the specified 5-to-30-minute range (rather than use one common value for all UEs). The randomization de-correlates timer expiry among rejected UEs, preventing a synchronized wave of renewed NAS/registration attempts and therefore avoiding a signalling surge that could prolong or recreate the congestion.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.3.7 (Congestion control), in particular the MO NAS-signalling congestion-control procedure (commonly clause 5.3.7.2 depending on release). It specifies random selection of T3346 in the 5-30 minute range for congestion handling, with the intent of avoiding simultaneous UE re-attempts.

results.question: What actions must a UE take regarding timer T3346 when it enters a new PLMN that is not equivalent to the PLMN where the timer was started?
results.reference: The UE shall stop timer T3346 when initiating 5GMM procedures in the new PLMN.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.3.9, Handling of NAS level mobility management congestion control
results.model_answer: The UE shall stop timer T3346 upon entering a new PLMN that is not equivalent to the PLMN in which T3346 was started. The back-off is therefore not carried over to that non-equivalent PLMN; the UE does not wait for T3346 expiry before accessing the new PLMN.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 10.2.2 (Timer T3346): the T3346 timer description specifies that, if the UE enters a new PLMN that is not equivalent to the PLMN where T3346 was started, the UE shall stop T3346. Related T3346 handling is also specified with REGISTRATION REJECT processing in clause 5.3.2.6.

results.question: When is a UE allowed to initiate 5GMM procedures even if timer T3346 is running or deactivated?
results.reference: The UE is allowed to initiate 5GMM procedures if it is configured for high priority access in the selected PLMN, or if it needs to initiate signalling for emergency services or emergency services fallback.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.3.9, Handling of NAS level mobility management congestion control
results.model_answer: T3346 is a congestion back-off restriction for ordinary 5GMM initiation. A UE may override it to initiate the applicable 5GMM procedure when it needs emergency services (for example, emergency registration/service) or when it is configured/authorized for high-priority access. If T3346 is deactivated (not running), it imposes no back-off restriction; normal 5GMM initiation rules apply. The override does not make arbitrary non-emergency, non-priority 5GMM requests permissible while T3346 runs.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, the UE handling of REGISTRATION REJECT and SERVICE REJECT with congestion/back-off (T3346), notably clauses 5.5.1.2.7 and 5.6.1.3.5 (clause numbering/title may vary by release). These specify T3346-based back-off and the exceptions for emergency services and UE high-priority access.

results.question: How does a UE determine the establishment cause for non-3GPP access when initiating an N1 NAS signalling connection?
results.reference: The UE must first determine one or more access identities as specified in subclause 4.5.2 and table 4.5.2.1. Then, it selects the establishment cause by checking the rules in table 4.7.2.2.1, based on the determined access identities and the event that triggered the connection initiation. Finally, it provides the selected establishment cause to the lower layers.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.7.2.2, Establishment cause for non-3GPP access
results.model_answer: For a UE-initiated N1 NAS signalling connection over non-3GPP access, the UE sets the establishment cause to "mo-Signalling". It does not apply the 3GPP-access RRC establishment-cause selection associated with radio connection establishment. The non-3GPP access function (for example, N3IWF) handles the corresponding access/N2 signalling toward the AMF.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.6.1.2 (UE-initiated N1 NAS signalling connection establishment). The non-3GPP-access-specific rule states that the UE shall set the establishment cause to "mo-Signalling".

results.question: What establishment cause for non-3GPP access is used if a UE in 5GMM-IDLE mode initiates a service request procedure while an MMTEL voice call is ongoing?
results.reference: The establishment cause is mapped to 'MO MMTel voice call' type access attempt.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.7.2.2, Establishment cause for non-3GPP access
results.model_answer: The UE uses the "mo-voice-call" establishment cause for the non-3GPP access connection establishment.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.6.1.2 (Service request initiation). It specifies that, when a UE in 5GMM-IDLE over non-3GPP access initiates service request in association with an ongoing MMTEL voice call, it shall use the "mo-voice-call" establishment cause.

results.question: According to the mapping rules, what should a UE do if an access attempt matches more than one rule for determining the establishment cause for non-3GPP access?
results.reference: The UE shall use the establishment cause for non-3GPP access corresponding to the lowest rule number in table 4.7.2.2.1.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.7.2.2, Establishment cause for non-3GPP access
results.model_answer: The UE shall apply the highest-priority applicable mapping rule—i.e., select the establishment cause associated with the first applicable rule in the specified rule order. It shall not combine causes or choose arbitrarily.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.5.1.2.1 (UE-initiated registration procedure—General), in the non-3GPP access establishment-cause mapping rules: where more than one rule applies, the establishment cause corresponding to the rule with the highest priority (the first applicable rule in the listed order) is used.

results.question: What establishment cause for non-3GPP access is mapped when a UE initiates a service request procedure in 5GMM-IDLE mode while an SMSoIP is ongoing, but no MMTEL voice or video calls are ongoing?
results.reference: The establishment cause is mapped to 'MO SMS over IP' type access attempt.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.7.2.2, Establishment cause for non-3GPP access
results.model_answer: MO SMS ("mo-SMS").
results.evidence: Most likely clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, §5.3.4.2 (Service request procedure initiation). It specifies that, for non-3GPP access, when the service request is due to an ongoing SMSoIP and no MMTEL voice or video call is ongoing, the UE maps the establishment cause to MO SMS.

results.question: What are the two alternative actions a UE must take if a service request for initiating an emergency PDU session is not accepted by the network and the UE remains in the same selected PLMN where the last attempt was made?
results.reference: The UE must either inform the upper layers of the procedure failure, or de-register locally (if not already de-registered) and attempt initial registration for emergency services.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.6.1.6, Service request procedure for initiating an emergency PDU session not accepted by the network
results.model_answer: The UE shall either (1) wait 5 minutes before making another attempt to initiate the emergency PDU session in that same selected PLMN, or (2) select another PLMN and attempt to initiate the emergency PDU session there.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.6.1.4 (Service request procedure rejection), in the emergency-PDU-session-specific UE behaviour for an unaccepted SERVICE REQUEST.

results.question: How does the UE proceed when a service request for an emergency PDU session fails due to the abnormal case specified in subclause 5.6.1.7, and the UE is still in the same selected PLMN?
results.reference: After performing the procedures in subclause 5.6.1.7, the UE must either inform the upper layers of the failure or de-register locally (if needed) and attempt initial registration for emergency services.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.6.1.6, Service request procedure for initiating an emergency PDU session not accepted by the network
results.model_answer: The UE shall initiate the registration procedure with the registration type set to "emergency registration". This applies when the emergency-PDU-session service request has failed under the abnormal-case handling and the UE remains in the same selected PLMN.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, subclause 5.6.1.7 (Abnormal cases for the service request procedure): the emergency-service-request failure handling requires the UE, if it is still in the same selected PLMN, to initiate a registration procedure with registration type "emergency registration".

results.question: What is the consequence of the UE informing its upper layers about the failure of a service request for an emergency PDU session, as noted in the clause?
results.reference: It can result in the upper layers requesting another emergency call attempt using domain selection as specified in 3GPP TS 23.167 and, for failures due to abnormal cases, also 3GPP TS 24.229.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.6.1.6, Service request procedure for initiating an emergency PDU session not accepted by the network
results.model_answer: It provides an explicit failure indication to the UE's upper layers for the emergency PDU session. NAS does not imply that emergency service is successfully continued; the upper layers can take emergency-specific recovery action, such as retrying/initiating a new connection attempt or selecting an alternative access or emergency-service method, subject to their implementation and applicable procedures.
results.evidence: Most likely TS 24.501 clause 5.6.1.5 (Service request rejected by the network / Service request failure handling): the UE is required to inform upper layers of the failure when the failed service request concerns an emergency PDU session. The normative consequence is the upper-layer notification; any subsequent recovery decision is an upper-layer matter, not an automatic NAS guarantee.

results.question: Under what condition must the UE perform the actions of informing upper layers or de-registering locally after a failed service request for an emergency PDU session?
results.reference: The UE must perform these actions only if it is in the same selected PLMN where the last service request (or SERVICE REQUEST message) was attempted.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.6.1.6, Service request procedure for initiating an emergency PDU session not accepted by the network
results.model_answer: If the service request procedure for an emergency PDU session fails, the UE shall inform upper layers that emergency services are not available. In addition, only if the UE is registered for emergency services only, it shall locally de-register from the network.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.6.1.5 (Abnormal cases in the UE) is the most likely evidence clause: it specifies the UE actions when a service request for an emergency PDU session fails, including upper-layer notification and local deregistration when the UE is registered for emergency services only.

results.question: What is the purpose of including the Operator-defined access category definitions IE in a message to the UE?
results.reference: To either assign new operator-defined access category definitions to the UE or delete the existing operator-defined access category definitions stored at the UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.19.17, Operator-defined access category definitions
results.model_answer: It provides the UE with the operator's definitions for operator-defined access categories, so that the UE can classify applicable mobile-originated traffic/access attempts into the correct access category and apply the corresponding Unified Access Control (UAC) or access-barring treatment. In other words, it makes the UE's access-category selection consistent with operator policy rather than relying only on standardized categories.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 9.11.3, "Operator-defined access category definitions" IE; its stated function is to provide the UE with operator-defined access-category definitions. The UE uses received definitions in the NAS access-control procedures specified in TS 24.501 clause 5.16 (Access control / Unified Access Control).

results.question: How can the network modify the operator-defined access category definitions stored in the UE using this IE?
results.reference: By including the IE in a message, the network can perform two actions: assign new definitions to the UE or delete the definitions currently present at the UE side.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.19.17, Operator-defined access category definitions
results.model_answer: The network modifies a stored operator-defined access category definition by sending the Operator-defined access category definitions IE containing a definition with the same access category number as the stored one. The UE replaces the existing stored definition for that access category number with the received definition.
results.evidence: Most likely TS 24.501 clause 5.16.4.1 (Access control / operator-defined access category definitions): an operator-defined access category definition is identified by its access category number; when the network provides a definition with the same access category number, the UE replaces the stored definition with the received one.

results.question: In what scenario would the network send the Operator-defined access category definitions IE to a UE?
results.reference: When the network needs to update the UE's configuration by either providing new operator-defined access category definitions for the UE to use or commanding the UE to clear any such definitions it has stored.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.19.17, Operator-defined access category definitions
results.model_answer: The network sends the Operator-defined access category definitions IE when the UE has indicated support for operator-defined access-category definitions in its 5GMM capability and the AMF needs to provision or update those definitions. It is typically delivered in a REGISTRATION ACCEPT, and may subsequently be updated using a CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 8.2.7 (REGISTRATION ACCEPT message content/conditional IE inclusion), together with the CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND message definition. The IE is conditionally included when the UE supports operator-defined access-category definitions and the network has definitions to provide to the UE.

results.question: What are the functional roles that the UE and AUSF may support when EAP-TTLS with two phases of authentication is used?
results.reference: The UE may support acting as EAP peer of EAP-TTLS with two phases of authentication and as peer of a legacy authentication protocol. The AUSF may support acting as EAP server of EAP-TTLS with two phases of authentication.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.2.3A.2, EAP-TTLS with two phases of authentication
results.model_answer: With EAP-TTLS, the UE may support the EAP peer role and the AUSF may support the EAP server role. This role assignment does not reverse between the two EAP-TTLS phases: the AUSF is the TLS/EAP-TTLS server endpoint, while the UE is the TLS/EAP-TTLS peer endpoint. Phase 1 establishes/authenticates the TLS tunnel (including server authentication and optionally client-certificate authentication); phase 2 carries the protected inner authentication exchange.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.2.2.3 (EAP-based authentication / EAP-TTLS-related text, clause numbering/title may vary by release). The relevant normative mapping is that the UE supports the EAP peer functional role and the AUSF supports the EAP server functional role when EAP-TTLS is used. RFC 5281 defines the two EAP-TTLS phases and preserves the client/peer versus server endpoint roles across them.

results.question: Under what conditions is the indication to use MSK for derivation of KAUSF not included after successful primary authentication and key agreement?
results.reference: The indication is not included if the UE is registering or registered for onboarding services in SNPN and using default UE credentials, or if the UE is not registering/registered for onboarding services and using credentials from the selected entry of the 'list of subscriber data'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.2.3A.2, EAP-TTLS with two phases of authentication
results.model_answer: The indication is not included when the successful EAP-based primary authentication method is EAP-AKA'. In that case, K_AUSF is derived using the EAP-AKA' CK'/IK'-based 5G key-derivation path, rather than from the EAP MSK. For 5G AKA there is no EAP-Success message in which such an indication could be carried.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.1.3.6 (Authentication result): the EAP-Success handling specifies the indication to use MSK for K_AUSF derivation and states that this indication shall not be included when EAP-AKA' is used.

results.question: How is the SUPI formatted when EAP-TTLS with two phases of authentication is used for primary authentication and key agreement in an SNPN?
results.reference: The SUPI is in the form of a SUPI with the SUPI format 'network specific identifier' containing a network-specific identifier.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.2.3A.2, EAP-TTLS with two phases of authentication
results.model_answer: With two-phase EAP-TTLS in an SNPN, the UE uses an NAI-form identity. The outer (phase-1) EAP-Identity is an anonymous NAI, i.e. "anonymous@<SNPN-realm>", so that the SUPI is not exposed before the TTLS tunnel is established. The actual SUPI is provided only in the protected phase-2 exchange, in NAI form: "<SUPI-user-part>@<SNPN-realm>". The realm identifies/routs to the SNPN; the user part represents the subscriber identity. Thus, the SUPI is protected by the TLS tunnel rather than being sent as the outer EAP identity.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.1.3.2 (EAP authentication), in the SNPN/EAP-TTLS two-phase-authentication provisions. This text specifies use of an anonymous outer identity for EAP-TTLS and conveyance of the SUPI in the protected inner/phase-2 authentication, using NAI formatting. The associated NAI syntax is defined by RFC 7542; SUPI and SNPN identifier semantics are defined in 3GPP TS 23.003/TS 23.501.

results.question: What additional requirements apply when EAP-TTLS with two phases of authentication is used for primary authentication and key agreement in an SNPN?
results.reference: Requirements in subclause 5.4.1.2.3A.1 shall apply in addition to requirements specified in 3GPP TS 33.501 annex U.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.2.3A.2, EAP-TTLS with two phases of authentication
results.model_answer: For an SNPN using two-phase EAP-TTLS, the network has to be authenticated by the UE in the TLS (outer) phase before the UE performs the inner/phase-2 authentication. The UE shall validate the EAP-TTLS server certificate and its binding to the selected SNPN. The credentials/identity used for the subscriber or credential-holder authentication are to be conveyed only inside the TLS-protected tunnel in phase 2; an outer identity, if sent for routing, must not expose those credentials. The EAP-TTLS exchange must complete as an EAP primary-authentication method and provide the EAP keying material used by the 5G authentication/key hierarchy; failure of either TLS/server authentication or the inner authentication causes primary authentication failure.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.1.2.2 (primary authentication and key agreement using EAP), including its SNPN-specific EAP-TTLS requirements; read together with the SNPN primary-authentication security requirements in 3GPP TS 33.501 and EAP-TTLS in RFC 5281.

results.question: How does a UE derive a packet filter for the UL direction from a received DL IPv4 TCP packet in an IPv4 PDU session?
results.reference: The UE creates a packet filter containing: 1) an IPv4 remote address component set to the source address of the DL packet, 2) an IPv4 local address component set to the destination address of the DL packet, and 3) a protocol identifier component set to the protocol field value (TCP).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.2.5.1.4.2, Derivation of packet filter for UL direction from DL user data packet
results.model_answer: {'condition': 'This is Reflective QoS behavior: if Reflective QoS is authorized for the PDU session/QoS flow and the UE receives the downlink packet with the Reflective QoS Indicator (RQI) set, the UE derives an uplink packet filter for the QoS flow carrying that packet.', 'derivation': 'For a received IPv4/TCP downlink packet with IPv4 source A, IPv4 destination B, TCP source port X, and TCP destination port Y, the derived UL filter matches the reverse flow: IPv4 source B (/32), IPv4 destination A (/32), protocol TCP (IP protocol number 6), TCP source/local port Y, and TCP destination/remote port X.', 'result': 'Thus, UL TCP packets from B:Y to A:X are mapped to the reflected QoS flow. The UE does not derive this merely from any downlink TCP packet; the applicable Reflective QoS authorization and received RQI are required.'}
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.7.5 (Reflective QoS), especially the UE behavior for deriving an uplink packet filter from a downlink IP packet received with RQI. The clause specifies reversal of the IP addresses and transport-layer ports and retention of the protocol identifier for the derived UL packet filter.

results.question: Under what condition for an ESP-protocol DL packet does the UE proceed to derive a UL packet filter, and what are the first two IPv4 components?
results.reference: The UE proceeds if an uplink IPSec SA corresponding to the downlink IPSec SA indicated in the security parameters index field of the DL packet exists. The first two components are: 1) IPv4 remote address set to the DL packet's source address, and 2) IPv4 local address set to the DL packet's destination address.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.2.5.1.4.2, Derivation of packet filter for UL direction from DL user data packet
results.model_answer: For a downlink IPv4 packet using ESP, the UE derives the uplink packet filter only when it can identify the corresponding uplink IPsec/ESP security association for that received downlink ESP packet. The first two IPv4 filter components are: (1) IPv4 remote address = the downlink packet's IPv4 source address, with an all-ones (/32) mask; and (2) IPv4 local address = the downlink packet's IPv4 destination address, with an all-ones (/32) mask.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.7.2.2 (UE behaviour for Reflective QoS), in the rules/table for deriving an uplink packet filter from a downlink IP packet, including the ESP-specific condition and the IPv4 remote/local-address packet-filter components.

results.question: When deriving a UL packet filter from a DL Ethernet frame carrying IPv4 data, what additional components must be added beyond the Ethernet-specific components?
results.reference: Beyond any Ethernet-specific components (like S-TAG VID, PCP/DEI, or Ethertype), the UE must also add the IP-specific components based on the contents of the IP header, as described for IPv4 packets in bullet a) of the clause.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.2.5.1.4.2, Derivation of packet filter for UL direction from DL user data packet
results.model_answer: Add the inner IPv4/transport packet-filter components: an IPv4 remote-address/mask component (from the DL source IPv4 address), the protocol-identifier component (the IPv4 Protocol field), and, when the protocol has ports, the local- and remote-port component(s) derived from the DL destination and source ports respectively. These are added in addition to the Ethernet MAC/VLAN/Ethertype components, with UL/DL directionality reversed as applicable.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.7.5 (Support of reflective QoS), specifically the UE behaviour for deriving an uplink packet filter from a downlink Ethernet frame. The clause requires Ethernet packet-filter components and, for an Ethernet payload carrying IPv4, the applicable IPv4 packet-filter components, including IPv4 remote address/mask, protocol identifier, and transport-layer port component(s).

results.question: For which PDU session types is it not possible to derive a UL packet filter from a DL user data packet?
results.reference: It is not possible to derive a UL packet filter from a DL packet for PDU sessions of types other than Ethernet, IPv4, IPv6, and IPv4v6.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.2.5.1.4.2, Derivation of packet filter for UL direction from DL user data packet
results.model_answer: It is not possible for Ethernet and Unstructured PDU session types. UL packet-filter derivation from a received DL user-data packet is applicable only to IP PDU session types (IPv4, IPv6, and IPv4v6).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.7.5 (QoS rules; reflective QoS handling), NOTE: it is not possible to derive an UL packet filter from a DL user-data packet for Ethernet and Unstructured PDU session types.

results.question: What is the purpose of the authentication and key agreement procedure for a 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay?
results.reference: The purpose is to authenticate the 5G ProSe remote UE initiated by the relay and to agree on the KAUSF_P and KNR_ProSe keys when security for 5G ProSe communication via the relay is performed over the control plane.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.5.4.1, General
results.model_answer: It authenticates the 5G ProSe UE-to-network Relay to the 5G network and establishes the relay’s security context/keying material for protected relay-service operation. It is not the Remote UE’s end-to-end NAS authentication; a Remote UE retains its own authentication and NAS security context with the network when it accesses the network via the relay.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.17.4, in the 5G ProSe UE-to-network Relay procedures (including its authentication-and-key-agreement subclause, release-dependent numbering). The stated procedural objective is relay authentication and establishment of security material/security context for the UE-to-network relay service.

results.question: How is the authentication and key agreement procedure for a 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay initiated?
results.reference: The procedure is initiated by the UE (the relay) when it receives a ProSe direct link establishment request from the 5G ProSe remote UE that includes the remote UE's SUCI, for establishing a secure PC5 unicast link.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.5.4.1, General
results.model_answer: It is network-initiated. After the UE is registered and authorized/configured to act as a 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay, the AMF starts the relay authentication-and-key-agreement exchange by sending an EAP-Request/5G-Start in a DL NAS TRANSPORT message to the relay UE. The relay responds with EAP-Response/5G-Start in UL NAS TRANSPORT, after which the EAP authentication (e.g. EAP-AKA') proceeds and the relevant relay security keys are derived.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.18 (5G ProSe UE-to-network relay procedures), read with clause 5.2.3.3 (EAP-based/secondary authentication procedure). The latter specifies the network initiation using DL NAS TRANSPORT carrying EAP-Request/5G-Start and the UE response using UL NAS TRANSPORT carrying EAP-Response/5G-Start.

results.question: What role does the network play in the authentication and key agreement procedure for a 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay?
results.reference: If the network decides to process the relay key request message, it initiates and controls the EAP-based authentication and key agreement procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.5.4.1, General
results.model_answer: The network is the trusted authentication/key-management authority. It authenticates and authorizes the 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay (and, where applicable, the remote UE) using the UE's 5G credentials, controls the AKA exchange carried through the relay path, and provides/derives the resulting security context and relay-specific keying material. The relay primarily transports the relevant NAS/authentication signalling; it is not a substitute for the 5G network authentication function and is not given the UE's long-term subscription credentials.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.12.2, "Authentication and key agreement for 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay" (subclause numbering can vary by release/version). This procedure specifies network-controlled authentication/authorization and establishment of the security context for the UE-to-network relay service.

results.question: How are EAP messages exchanged during the authentication procedure for a 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay?
results.reference: The exchanges of EAP messages between the 5G ProSe remote UE and the network are relayed by the UE (the 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.5.4.1, General
results.model_answer: EAP is exchanged end-to-end between the 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay (the EAP peer) and the network-side EAP/AAA function, with the AMF/NAS acting as the transport path. Network-originated EAP-Request packets are delivered to the relay UE in downlink NAS transport, and the relay UE returns the corresponding EAP-Response packets in uplink NAS transport. This request/response transport is repeated for as many EAP rounds as required; EAP-Success or EAP-Failure terminates the relay-authentication exchange. The EAP exchange is NAS/N1 based and is not carried over PC5 to a remote UE.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 4.13.2.3, "Authentication procedure for 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay" (clause numbering/title can vary by release). The clause specifies that EAP messages for this procedure are exchanged between the 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay and the network using UL NAS TRANSPORT and DL NAS TRANSPORT messages.

results.question: What actions should a UE take upon the first expiry of timer T3580 when the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST was sent with request type set to 'initial emergency request'?
results.reference: The UE may either inform the upper layers of the procedure failure, which could trigger another emergency call attempt via domain selection, or locally de-register (if not already) and attempt initial registration for emergency services.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.4.1.6, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: On the first expiry of T3580, the UE shall retransmit the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST and restart T3580. The retransmitted request shall be identical to the original request except that the Request type shall be changed from "initial emergency request" to "existing emergency PDU session".
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.3.2.2 (UE-requested PDU session establishment procedure): on the first expiry of T3580, the UE retransmits the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST and restarts T3580; where the original Request type was "initial emergency request", the retransmitted message uses Request type "existing emergency PDU session".

results.question: How does a UE handle the collision when it receives a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND with the same PDU session ID after sending a PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST for a handover of an existing emergency PDU session between accesses?
results.reference: The UE proceeds with the UE-requested PDU session establishment procedure and aborts the network-requested PDU session modification procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.4.1.6, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: The UE shall not abort the pending PDU session establishment procedure in this exceptional case. It processes the received PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND according to the normal network-initiated modification procedure (including sending the applicable PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMPLETE), while continuing the establishment procedure for the handover of the existing emergency PDU session between accesses. This is an exception to the normal collision rule, under which receipt of a modification command for the same PDU session ID causes the pending establishment procedure to be aborted.
results.evidence: Most likely: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.4.2.4 (network-initiated PDU session modification procedure), collision handling text for receipt of a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND while a PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST is pending for the same PDU session ID. The clause specifies the exception where the establishment request is for handover of an existing emergency PDU session between 3GPP and non-3GPP access: the UE shall not abort the establishment procedure.

results.question: What is the UE behavior if timer T3580 expires for the first time and the request type was not an emergency type, and what limits apply to retransmissions?
results.reference: The UE retransmits the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST message along with the original PDU session information, resets and restarts timer T3580 if needed. This retransmission can be repeated up to four times.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.4.1.6, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: On the first expiry of T3580, if the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST did not carry an emergency request type, the UE retransmits the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST and restarts T3580. Retransmission is permitted only while T3580 has expired fewer than five times; consequently, the UE can make at most four retransmissions after the initial transmission. On the fifth expiry, or for an emergency request type, the UE aborts the PDU session establishment procedure rather than retransmitting.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.4.1 (UE-requested PDU session establishment procedure), T3580 expiry handling: the UE retransmits and restarts T3580 when the timer has expired fewer than five times and the request type is not an emergency request; otherwise it aborts the procedure. This limits retransmissions to four.

results.question: In a collision scenario where the UE receives a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND after sending a PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST for establishing user plane resources on a second access for an existing MA PDU session, how should the UE proceed?
results.reference: The UE shall proceed with both the UE-requested PDU session establishment procedure and the network-requested PDU session modification procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.4.1.6, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: The UE shall abort the pending PDU session establishment procedure that was initiated to establish user-plane resources on the second access of the existing MA PDU session, and shall process the received PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND according to the network-requested PDU session modification procedure. It does not continue the colliding second-access establishment procedure.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.4.2.5 (PDU session establishment collision handling; clause numbering can vary slightly by release): the UE receiving a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND for a PDU session for which it sent a PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST to establish user-plane resources over a second access for an MA PDU session shall abort the PDU session establishment procedure and process the PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND.

results.question: What potential delay is noted for initial uplink NAS message transmission in a specific access scenario, and what causes it?
results.reference: In a satellite NG-RAN access, transmission can be delayed by up to 100 seconds due to a GNSS fix time in lower layers when in a GNSS cold state.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.1.1, General
results.model_answer: For 3GPP access when the UE is CM-IDLE, transmission of the initial uplink NAS message can be delayed until an RRC connection is established. The delay is caused by the access-stratum connection-establishment steps—typically random access and RRC setup—needed to create the NAS signalling connection; it is not an inherent NAS-message processing delay.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.3.3.1 (NAS signalling connection establishment, general), read with the UE-initiated registration/service-request procedures. It specifies that, for 3GPP access, establishment of the NAS signalling connection involves RRC connection establishment when the UE is CM-IDLE; consequently the initial NAS message cannot be delivered immediately.

results.question: Beyond its main function, what additional role does the 5GMM sublayer fulfill?
results.reference: A further function is to provide connection management services to other sublayer(s).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.1.1, General
results.model_answer: In addition to mobility management, the 5GMM sublayer fulfills connection-management functions—i.e., it controls NAS signalling connectivity between the UE and the 5G core.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 4.2.1 (General): the 5GMM sublayer provides control-plane functions related to mobility management and connection management.

results.question: How many times shall the AMF retransmit the NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION COMMAND message upon timer T3575 expiry before aborting the procedure?
results.reference: The AMF shall retransmit the message four times, and on the fifth expiry of timer T3575, it shall abort the procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.7.2.3, Abnormal cases on the network side
results.model_answer: 4 times. The AMF retransmits the NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION COMMAND on the first through fourth expiries of T3575; on the fifth expiry it aborts the network slice-specific authentication procedure.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.8.2 (network slice-specific authentication procedure): the AMF shall retransmit the NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION COMMAND and restart T3575 on expiry; upon the fifth expiry of T3575, the AMF shall abort the procedure.

results.question: Under what condition related to handover shall the AMF retransmit the NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION COMMAND message after a lower layers indication of non-delivery?
results.reference: The AMF shall retransmit the message if it could not be delivered due to an intra AMF handover and the target TAI is included in the TAI list, upon successful completion of the handover.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.7.2.3, Abnormal cases on the network side
results.model_answer: The AMF shall retransmit the NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION COMMAND only if no handover procedure is ongoing for the UE (i.e., the UE is not in handover) when the lower layers report non-delivery.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.15.8.2 (network slice-specific authentication procedure): on a lower-layers non-delivery indication for a NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION COMMAND, retransmission is required if the UE is not in a handover procedure.

results.question: What action shall the network take if a DEREGISTRATION REQUEST message is received with the same access type as an ongoing network slice-specific authentication and authorization procedure?
results.reference: The network shall abort the ongoing network slice-specific authentication and authorization procedure and progress the UE-initiated de-registration procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.7.2.3, Abnormal cases on the network side
results.model_answer: The network shall abort the ongoing network slice-specific authentication and authorization procedure and process the DEREGISTRATION REQUEST (i.e., proceed with deregistration) for that access type.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.15.14 (Network slice-specific authentication and authorization procedure): if a DEREGISTRATION REQUEST is received with the same access type as an ongoing network slice-specific authentication and authorization procedure, the network shall abort that procedure and perform the deregistration procedure.

results.question: How does the network handle a collision between a network slice-specific authentication procedure and a deregistration request with a different access type?
results.reference: The network shall proceed with both procedures concurrently when the access type in the DEREGISTRATION REQUEST message is different from the one used for the ongoing authentication procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.7.2.3, Abnormal cases on the network side
results.model_answer: The network handles the procedures independently. If it receives a DEREGISTRATION REQUEST for an access type different from the access type on which network slice-specific authentication (NSSAA) is ongoing, the AMF processes the deregistration for that other access type, but does not abort the ongoing NSSAA procedure. NSSAA continues for its original access type/S-NSSAI context.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.15.8.2 (network slice-specific authentication procedure), collision-handling text for receipt of a DEREGISTRATION REQUEST with a different access type. The rule is that the network continues the network slice-specific authentication procedure when the deregistration concerns a different access type.

results.question: How should the UE proceed when it experiences a transmission failure of the NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION COMPLETE message and the current TAI is not in the TAI list?
results.reference: The UE shall abort the network slice-specific authentication and authorization procedure. If in 5GMM-REGISTERED state, it initiates a registration procedure for mobility and periodic registration update with 'mobility registration updating' in the 5GS registration type IE; otherwise, it initiates a registration procedure for initial registration.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.7.2.4, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: The UE shall initiate the registration procedure with registration type "mobility registration updating". It should not use a service request while the current TAI is outside the stored TAI list; the registration update re-establishes valid registration/location context before the NSSAA exchange can continue.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.15.5.2 (network slice-specific authentication and authorization/NSSAA procedure, UE behavior following failure to transmit NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION COMPLETE). The applicable branch states that, when transmission of this message fails and the current TAI is not in the TAI list, the UE initiates a mobility registration updating procedure.

results.question: What determines the UE's behavior when a transmission failure of the NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION COMPLETE message occurs without a change in the current TAI?
results.reference: The UE implementation decides how to re-run the ongoing procedure that triggered the network slice-specific authentication and authorization procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.7.2.4, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: If the current TAI has not changed, the UE retransmits the NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION COMPLETE message and continues the network slice-specific authentication procedure (including the applicable T3580 handling). A mobility-registration update is relevant only when the current TAI has changed.
results.evidence: Most likely: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.15.14 (Network slice-specific authentication and authorization), UE procedure for NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION COMPLETE and its transmission failure; see also the T3580 procedure in clause 5.4.7. The operative condition is whether the current TAI changed: no TAI change leads to retransmission of the COMPLETE message rather than registration updating.

results.question: Under what condition should the UE ignore a received NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION COMMAND message during a de-registration procedure collision?
results.reference: The UE shall ignore the NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION COMMAND message if it is received after sending a DEREGISTRATION REQUEST message and the access type in the DEREGISTRATION REQUEST is the same as the access in which the command message is received.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.7.2.4, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: The UE shall ignore a received NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION COMMAND if a de-registration procedure is already in progress (i.e., the command collides with de-registration). The UE continues the de-registration procedure rather than starting or continuing network slice-specific authentication.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.15.8, "Network slice-specific authentication and authorization", in the UE procedure/collision-handling text for receipt of a NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION COMMAND. It specifies that, when a de-registration procedure is in progress, the UE ignores this command.

results.question: How does the UE handle a collision between the network slice-specific authentication and authorization procedure and the de-registration procedure when the access types differ?
results.reference: The UE shall proceed with both procedures when the access type included in the DEREGISTRATION REQUEST message is different from the access in which the NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION COMMAND message is received.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.7.2.4, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: When the network slice-specific authentication and authorization (NSSAA) procedure and de-registration concern different access types, the UE does not treat them as conflicting. The UE continues the ongoing NSSAA procedure for its associated access type and performs the de-registration procedure for the other access type independently. NSSAA is aborted because of de-registration only when both procedures apply to the same access type.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.15.8.6 (Collision handling) is the most likely evidence clause. It specifies the UE collision behavior between NSSAA and de-registration: the NSSAA procedure is aborted for a de-registration on the same access type; where the access types differ, the UE continues the NSSAA procedure.

results.question: What three components must be associated with each NSAG ID within the NSAG information provided by the UE NAS layer?
results.reference: Each NSAG ID must be associated with: a) a list of S-NSSAIs from the configured NSSAI, b) an NSAG area defined by a list of TAIs where the S-NSSAI to NSAG ID mapping is valid, and c) a priority value for that NSAG ID.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.6.2.6, Provision of NSAG information to lower layers
results.model_answer: Each NSAG ID is associated with: (1) one or more S-NSSAIs, (2) an NSAG priority, and (3) an NSAG DRX cycle.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.15.16, Network slice AS group information: the UE NAS layer provides NSAG information to the UE AS layer, with each NSAG ID associated with S-NSSAI(s), an NSAG priority, and an NSAG DRX cycle.

results.question: How does the UE NAS layer determine which S-NSSAIs to include in the list associated with an NSAG ID?
results.reference: The UE NAS layer must include only the S-NSSAIs that are part of the configured NSSAI in the list associated with each NSAG ID.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.6.2.6, Provision of NSAG information to lower layers
results.model_answer: The UE NAS layer does not infer NSAG membership from the SST/SD, Requested NSSAI, or URSP. It uses the network-provided NSAG information: for each NSAG ID, the UE associates exactly the S-NSSAIs explicitly listed with that NSAG ID and stores/updates that association. Thus, the list for an NSAG ID is the S-NSSAI list carried in the corresponding NSAG-information entry; the UE should not add other S-NSSAIs merely because they are configured, requested, allowed, or mapped NSSAIs.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.15.15, "Support for network slice admission control" (clause numbering can vary by release). Its UE behavior for received NSAG information is to associate the NSAG ID with the S-NSSAIs contained in the received list, i.e. the association is explicitly network signalled rather than locally derived by NAS.

results.question: Under what condition is the UE NAS layer required to provide NSAG information to the lower layers, and what specific version of this information must be provided?
results.reference: When NSAG information is available, the UE NAS layer is required to provide it to the lower layers, and it must provide the most recent version of the NSAG information.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.6.2.6, Provision of NSAG information to lower layers
results.model_answer: The UE NAS layer shall provide NSAG information to lower layers when it receives NSAG information from the network in a REGISTRATION ACCEPT message (including an update of previously stored NSAG information). It shall provide the NSAG information corresponding to the NSAG information version received from the network—i.e., the latest/current received NSAG-information version, not an older stored version.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.5.1.2.4, UE processing of REGISTRATION ACCEPT. The normative processing associated with the NSAG information IE requires the UE to pass the received NSAG information to lower layers, using the received NSAG-information version.

results.question: What is the purpose of the NSAG area, defined by a list of TAIs, that is associated with each NSAG ID?
results.reference: The NSAG area specifies the geographical area, identified by the list of TAIs, where the mapping between the associated S-NSSAI(s) and the NSAG ID is valid and applicable.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.6.2.6, Provision of NSAG information to lower layers
results.model_answer: The NSAG area scopes the applicability of an NSAG ID geographically. Its TAI list identifies the tracking areas in which that NSAG ID is valid/usable for Network Slice Admission Control; the UE uses the current TAI to determine whether the associated NSAG information applies. It is therefore an admission-control applicability area, not by itself a mobility restriction or slice-authorization area.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.15.x, "Network Slice Admission Control", in the NSAG-information description: an NSAG area is a list of TAIs associated with an NSAG ID and indicates the area where that NSAG ID applies. The corresponding NAS IE definition is in clause 9.11.3.x, "NSAG information".

results.question: What determines the inclusion of the UE's usage setting information element in the protocol?
results.reference: The inclusion is determined by whether the UE has IMS voice capability.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.6.14, UE's usage setting
results.model_answer: In a REGISTRATION REQUEST, inclusion is determined by the UE's configured usage setting: a UE configured for voice-centric usage shall include the UE's usage setting IE; a UE configured for data-centric usage shall not include it. Thus, presence of the IE signals the voice-centric setting in this procedure.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 8.2.6.1 (REGISTRATION REQUEST message content), under the UE's usage setting IE conditionality: the UE includes the IE when configured for voice-centric usage and does not include it when configured for data-centric usage. See also clause 9.11.3.54 (UE's usage setting IE encoding/semantics).

results.question: How does a UE's support for IMS voice relate to the presence of the UE's usage setting IE?
results.reference: If the UE supports IMS voice, then the UE's usage setting IE shall be included in the message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.6.14, UE's usage setting
results.model_answer: In a normal REGISTRATION REQUEST, support for IMS voice over PS sessions requires the UE to include the UE's usage setting IE. Thus, presence of this IE indicates that the UE supports IMS voice over PS sessions; its value then indicates whether the UE is voice-centric or data-centric. Conversely, a UE not supporting IMS voice over PS sessions does not include the IE. Absence is not an unconditional proof of no support, because emergency-registration-specific rules can prohibit its inclusion.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.5.1.2.2 (REGISTRATION REQUEST message content/handling), states in substance: a UE supporting IMS voice over PS sessions shall include the UE's usage setting IE in the REGISTRATION REQUEST. The IE semantics are specified in clause 9.11.3.54 (UE's usage setting).

results.question: In which specific message type is the EAP message IE included to convey EAP-failure?
results.reference: It is included in the REGISTRATION REJECT message when that message is used for conveying EAP-failure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.9.4, EAP message
results.model_answer: The EAP message IE conveys an EAP-Failure in the 5GMM AUTHENTICATION REJECT message (message type 0x58).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 8.2.24 ("Authentication reject message"; clause numbering can vary by release): for EAP-based authentication, the EAP message IE included in an AUTHENTICATION REJECT message shall contain an EAP-Failure message.

results.question: What entity performs network slice admission control on the S-NSSAI during the PDU session establishment procedure, and what action does it take if the maximum number of PDU sessions for that slice has been reached?
results.reference: The SMF performs network slice admission control during PDU session establishment. If the maximum number of PDU sessions for the network slice associated with the S-NSSAI has already been reached, the SMF rejects the PDU session establishment request using S-NSSAI based congestion control as specified in subclauses 6.2.8 and 6.4.1.4.2.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.6.3.1, Session management based network slice admission control
results.model_answer: The AMF performs network-slice admission control for the requested S-NSSAI. If the maximum permitted number of PDU sessions for that S-NSSAI has been reached, the AMF rejects the request by sending a PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REJECT with 5GSM cause #65, "maximum number of PDU sessions reached."
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.4.1.2 (UE-requested PDU session establishment). It specifies AMF handling of the requested S-NSSAI, including network-slice admission control and rejection with 5GSM cause #65 when the maximum number of PDU sessions for the S-NSSAI is reached.

results.question: How does operator policy affect the application of session management based network slice admission control for PDU sessions used for emergency services or priority services?
results.reference: Based on operator policy, the session management based network slice admission control is either not applicable for such PDU sessions, or the result of the control is ignored for them.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.6.3.1, Session management based network slice admission control
results.model_answer: TS 24.501 leaves the applicability of session-management-based network slice admission control (SM-NSAC) to PDU sessions used for emergency services or priority services to operator policy. Thus, such sessions are not categorically exempt or categorically subject to SM-NSAC: the UE applies the SM-NSAC rules only when the operator policy requires it. This policy choice governs admission-control handling, not the identification of a session as emergency or priority service.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.15.5.2, "Session management based network slice admission control". Relevant normative wording is: "Whether the UE applies session management based network slice admission control to a PDU session used for emergency services or priority services is based on operator policy."

results.question: For which two specific types of PDU sessions does the clause state that session management based network slice admission control is not applicable?
results.reference: The control is not applicable to PDU sessions established for emergency services (based on operator policy) and to PDU sessions established for onboarding services in an SNPN.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.6.3.1, Session management based network slice admission control
results.model_answer: It is not applicable to (1) PDU sessions requested with request type "initial emergency request" and (2) PDU sessions requested with request type "existing emergency PDU session"—i.e., emergency PDU sessions, including continuation of an existing emergency PDU session.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.15.5 (Network slice admission control), in the session-management-based network-slice-admission-control description: it excludes PDU sessions with the emergency request types "initial emergency request" and "existing emergency PDU session".

results.question: What is the purpose of sending a 5GSM STATUS message according to the 6.5.1 clause?
results.reference: The purpose is to report certain error conditions detected upon receipt of 5GSM protocol data at any time.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.5.1, General
results.model_answer: According to TS 24.501 clause 6.5.1, a 5GSM STATUS message is sent by the UE or the network to report certain 5GSM protocol error conditions. It supports the 5GSM status procedure and may be initiated at any time.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.5.1 (General): "The 5GSM status procedure can be initiated by the UE or the network at any time. The 5GSM STATUS message is used to report certain error conditions."

results.question: Under what condition is a 5GSM STATUS message sent, as specified in the clause?
results.reference: It is sent when certain error conditions are detected upon receipt of 5GSM protocol data.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.5.1, General
results.model_answer: A 5GSM STATUS message is sent by the UE or network when it detects a protocol error in a 5GSM message that cannot be handled by the procedure specified for that corresponding 5GSM message.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.4.4 (5GSM status procedure): the procedure may be initiated when a protocol error is detected; specifically, a 5GSM STATUS message is sent when the detected protocol error cannot be handled by the procedure defined for the corresponding 5GSM message.

results.question: How does the SMF initiate the PDU EAP message reliable transport procedure?
results.reference: The SMF creates a PDU SESSION AUTHENTICATION COMMAND message, sets specific IEs (PTI to 'No procedure transaction identity assigned', EAP message to the provided/generated EAP-request, Remote UE handling information to the remote user identity if received), sends the message, and starts timer T3590.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.1.2.1, PDU EAP message reliable transport procedure initiation
results.model_answer: The SMF initiates PDU EAP reliable transport by sending an EAP-Request to the UE in a PDU SESSION AUTHENTICATION COMMAND NAS SM message for the relevant PDU session. It delivers the N1 SM message via the AMF, which forwards it to the UE (normally encapsulated in a DL NAS TRANSPORT). The UE acknowledges/responds with PDU SESSION AUTHENTICATION COMPLETE carrying the EAP-Response; this request/response exchange provides the reliable transport mechanism, including retransmission/error handling where applicable.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.10.5 (PDU session authentication procedure), in particular the subclause describing PDU EAP message reliable transport (subclause numbering may vary by release). The normative behavior is that the SMF sends a PDU SESSION AUTHENTICATION COMMAND containing an EAP-Request message to initiate the procedure, and the UE returns a PDU SESSION AUTHENTICATION COMPLETE containing the EAP-Response.

results.question: What actions does the UE take regarding timers T3584 and T3585 upon receiving a PDU SESSION AUTHENTICATION COMMAND message?
results.reference: If timers T3585 (associated with the S-NSSAI or no S-NSSAI) and T3584 (associated with the DNN/no DNN and S-NSSAI/no S-NSSAI) are running for the established PDU session context, the UE stops both timers.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.1.2.1, PDU EAP message reliable transport procedure initiation
results.model_answer: Upon receipt of a PDU SESSION AUTHENTICATION COMMAND, the UE shall stop timer T3584 and timer T3585, if either timer is running.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.4.1.5 (PDU session authentication procedure), UE handling of PDU SESSION AUTHENTICATION COMMAND: the UE stops T3584 and T3585, if running.

results.question: How does the UE handle the EAP message when it receives a PDU SESSION AUTHENTICATION COMMAND message via NAS transport?
results.reference: The UE passes the EAP message from the EAP message IE to the upper layers using the NAS transport procedure. Apart from this and stopping relevant timers, the DN-initiated procedure is transparent to the UE's 5GSM layer.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.1.2.1, PDU EAP message reliable transport procedure initiation
results.model_answer: The UE NAS/5GSM entity extracts the EAP message from the PDU SESSION AUTHENTICATION COMMAND (received as N1 SM information in a DL NAS TRANSPORT) and delivers it to the UE EAP peer for EAP processing; NAS does not itself perform the EAP method. Any EAP response produced by the EAP peer is carried by the UE in a PDU SESSION AUTHENTICATION COMPLETE message, sent to the network in UL NAS TRANSPORT for the same PDU session. EAP Success/Failure is handled by the EAP peer and determines the authentication result.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.4.1.2, network-initiated PDU session authentication procedure (UE handling of PDU SESSION AUTHENTICATION COMMAND): the UE passes the received EAP message to the EAP peer and sends the EAP peer's response, when applicable, in PDU SESSION AUTHENTICATION COMPLETE. See also the PDU SESSION AUTHENTICATION COMMAND/COMPLETE message definitions and the EAP message IE.

results.question: What specific UE timer action is triggered by receiving a PDU SESSION AUTHENTICATION COMMAND message when the UE had provided a DNN during PDU session establishment?
results.reference: The UE stops timer T3396 if it is running for that specific DNN provided by the UE during the PDU session establishment.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.1.2.1, PDU EAP message reliable transport procedure initiation
results.model_answer: The UE stops T3580 (if it is running) on receipt of the PDU SESSION AUTHENTICATION COMMAND. After sending PDU SESSION AUTHENTICATION COMPLETE, it starts/restarts T3580 to await the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT ACCEPT or REJECT. The DNN supplied in the establishment request identifies the requested PDU session/authentication context; it does not change the timer identity.
results.evidence: Most likely clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.4.2 (PDU session authentication procedure; UE handling of PDU SESSION AUTHENTICATION COMMAND), read together with clause 6.4.1 (PDU session establishment procedure) and the T3580 timer definition. The UE-side procedure specifies stopping T3580 upon command reception and starting T3580 after transmitting PDU SESSION AUTHENTICATION COMPLETE.

results.question: How does the NAS protocol ensure the transport of messages for session management between the UE and the network?
results.reference: It carries SM messages between the UE and the SMF, transported transparently through the AMF, to manage the establishment, modification, and release of PDU sessions.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.1, Overview
results.model_answer: 5G session-management (5GSM) messages are carried over the NAS interface by encapsulating them in 5GMM NAS transport messages. The UE places a 5GSM message in the Payload container IE of an UL NAS TRANSPORT message, identifies the PDU session with the PDU session ID, and sends it to the AMF. The AMF uses the PDU session context and/or routing information such as S-NSSAI and DNN to forward the N1 SM information to the appropriate SMF. In the downlink, the SMF provides N1 SM information to the AMF, which encapsulates it in a DL NAS TRANSPORT message for delivery to the UE. NAS security protection (integrity, and ciphering when activated) protects these NAS transport messages according to the active NAS security context.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 8.2.1 (NAS transport general): NAS transport procedures are used to transport 5GSM messages between the UE and the SMF; UL NAS TRANSPORT and DL NAS TRANSPORT carry the 5GSM message as N1 SM information in the Payload container.

results.question: What specific 5GSM cause value should the SMF set in the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REJECT message when rejecting connectivity because the requested service option is not subscribed by the user?
results.reference: The SMF should set the 5GSM cause IE to value #33, which corresponds to 'requested service option not subscribed'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.4.1.4.1, General
results.model_answer: Set 5GSM cause value 33 (0x21), "requested service option not subscribed".
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 9.11.4.2 (5GSM cause values): cause #33 is defined as "requested service option not subscribed". This cause is carried in the 5GSM cause IE of the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REJECT message.

results.question: How should a UE behave upon receiving a PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REJECT with cause #86, if it had not initially included the CAA-level UAV ID in its request?
results.reference: The UE must not send another request for UAS services without including the CAA-level UAV ID in the service-level device ID of the Service-level-AA container IE. Furthermore, for any subsequent upper layer request to establish a PDU session for UAS services, the UE must initiate the procedure by including the CAA-level UAV ID in that specific field.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.4.1.4.1, General
results.model_answer: The UE shall initiate a new UE-requested PDU session establishment procedure and include the CAA-level UAV ID in the new PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST. This handling is triggered by 5GSM cause #86 when the CAA-level UAV ID was absent from the rejected request; the UE does not merely retransmit the same request without the ID.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.4.1.4 (UE handling of PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REJECT during UE-requested PDU session establishment), including the condition for 5GSM cause #86 and an initially omitted CAA-level UAV ID. The 5GSM cause coding is specified in clause 9.11.4.2 (5GSM cause).

results.question: According to the clause, what are two distinct 5GSM cause values that the SMF could use to indicate a problem specifically related to the PDU session type requested by the UE?
results.reference: The SMF could use cause #28 'unknown PDU session type' or cause #50 'PDU session type IPv4 only allowed'. Other valid examples from the list include #51, #57, #58, and #61.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.4.1.4.1, General
results.model_answer: 5GSM cause #50, "PDU session type IPv4 only allowed," and 5GSM cause #51, "PDU session type IPv6 only allowed." They indicate that the UE-requested PDU session type is not permitted because the SMF allows only IPv4 or only IPv6, respectively.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.7.1 (5GSM cause): cause value 50 is defined as "PDU session type IPv4 only allowed" and cause value 51 as "PDU session type IPv6 only allowed."

results.question: When the network rejects a PDU session establishment due to the UE being outside the valid service area for a Local Area Data Network, which 5GSM cause value from the provided list must be indicated in the rejection?
results.reference: The SMF must set the 5GSM cause IE to value #46, which corresponds to 'out of LADN service area'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.4.1.4.1, General
results.model_answer: 5GSM cause #64, "UE not in LADN service area", shall be indicated in the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REJECT.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.4.1.2 (UE-requested PDU session establishment procedure): when the UE is outside the valid service area of the requested LADN, the network rejects the request using 5GSM cause #64 "UE not in LADN service area". The cause-value assignment is specified in clause 9.11.4.2 (5GSM cause).

results.question: Under what conditions may a UE include the Requested PEIPS assistance information IE?
results.reference: The UE may include it only if the UE supports NR paging subgrouping, is not performing initial registration for emergency services, is not currently registered for emergency services, and does not have an active emergency PDU session.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.6.38, Requested PEIPS assistance information
results.model_answer: A UE may include the Requested PEIPS assistance information IE in a REGISTRATION REQUEST when it supports PEIPS (Paging Early Indication with Paging Subgrouping) and wants the network to provide PEIPS assistance information. The IE is a request for such assistance; it is not applicable merely because PEIPS exists in the network. Normal REGISTRATION REQUEST applicability and encoding rules also apply.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 8.2.6.1 (REGISTRATION REQUEST message content), in the entry/text for the "Requested PEIPS assistance information" IE. The associated UE registration-procedure text is in clause 5.5.1.2.2 (UE-initiated registration procedure).
